Idempotency on the sending side is per payout and status, so one status produces one delivery per endpoint. Resending an approval code or adding a note produces no event.

| Database `status` | `X-Recv-Event` / `event_type` | Payload `status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pending-approval`, `pending-otp-verification` | `payout.pending-approval` | `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `PENDING_OTP_VERIFICATION` |
| `pending` | `payout.approved` | `PENDING` |
| `initiated` | `payout.initiated` | `INITIATED` |
| `sent` | `payout.sent` | `SENT` |
| `processed` | `payout.processed` | `PROCESSED` |
| `failed` | `payout.failed` | `FAILED` |
| `rejected` | `payout.rejected` | `REJECTED` |
| `cancelled` | `payout.cancelled` | `CANCELLED` |

The payload `status` is the database status in upper case with underscores, so it does not always match the event name (`payout.approved` carries `PENDING`).

```json
{
  "event_type": "payout.sent",
  "payout_id": 120,
  "network": "SOLANA",
  "token": "USDC",
  "amount": "100",
  "amount_usd": "100.000000",
  "email": "test@test.com",
  "address": "9xQeWvG816bUx9EPjHmaT23yvVM2ZWbrrpZb9PusVFin",
  "from_address": "HotWa11etAddre55xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "tx_hash": "5KjP2n8vQ4wR7tY1uI3oA6sD9fG2hJ4kL7zX0cV5bN8mQ1wE3rT6yU9iO2pA5sD8f",
  "status": "SENT",
  "withdrawal_type": "payout_merchant",
  "currency_type": "token",
  "created_at": 1750340081,
  "updated_at": 1750340282,
  "timestamp": 1750340282,
  "failure_reason": "",
  "network_fee_raw": "5000"
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event_type` | string | The event name, same as `X-Recv-Event`. |
| `payout_id` | integer | The payout `id`. |
| `network` | string | `SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`. |
| `token` | string | Currency code. |
| `amount` | string | Token amount. |
| `amount_usd` | string | USD value at creation, six decimals. |
| `email` | string | Recipient email. |
| `address` | string | Destination. |
| `from_address` | string | Hot wallet address, or `""` before assignment. |
| `tx_hash` | string | Transaction hash, or `""` before broadcast. |
| `status` | string | Upper-case database status. |
| `withdrawal_type` | string | Always `payout_merchant`. |
| `currency_type` | string | `native` or `token`. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `timestamp` | integer | Unix seconds: creation, last update, and when the event was recorded. |
| `failure_reason` | string | Reason on `failed`, otherwise `""`. |
| `network_fee_raw` | string or null | Actual network fee in base units of the native token once known. Not part of PayRam's payload. |

Handle payout events like payment events: verify the signature, deduplicate on `X-Recv-Delivery`, and expect duplicates and out-of-order arrivals. The `initiated` event is committed before the broadcast is attempted, so an `initiated` followed by nothing for a while means the worker is waiting for confirmations or for the next attempt, not that the payout was lost; read the payout to see its current status.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction.md

# Deployment guide

recv.fund runs on a Linux server you control. There are three ways to get it running.

| Method | When to use it | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-line script | Most installs. The script installs Docker if needed, asks a few questions, writes the compose project and starts it. | [Quick setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/quick-setup.md) |
| Manual docker compose | You want to write the compose file and `.env` yourself, run behind your own proxy, or use an external Postgres. | [Advanced setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md) |
| Developer build from source | You have a source checkout and want to build the images locally instead of pulling them. Only available to people with source access. | [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md) (`--source`) |

Whichever method you pick, the result is the same `docker compose` project: Caddy on ports 80 and 443, the API, the web app, Redis, and either a bundled or an external Postgres.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Operating system | Ubuntu, Debian, Linux Mint, CentOS, RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, Fedora, Arch Linux or Alpine Linux, on amd64 or arm64. macOS with Docker Desktop for local testing over plain HTTP only. |
| CPU | 2 cores |
| Memory | 4 GB |
| Disk | 20 GB recommended. The installer warns below 10 GB and asks before continuing below 5 GB. |
| Ports | 80 and 443 free for Let's Encrypt, or one free port behind your own reverse proxy (see `--http-port`) |
| Time | About ten minutes |

The server needs outbound access to the chain RPC endpoints and, for mainnet prices of SOL and ETH, to CoinGecko.

## Mainnet or testnet

Every install runs against one network type. Choose it at install time; it cannot be switched later without a reset.

- `testnet`: Solana devnet and Robinhood Chain testnet. Every payment is a test payment. Use this for a first install.
- `mainnet`: Solana mainnet and Robinhood Chain mainnet. Real funds.

## What to back up

Three things: the database, the `api-uploads` volume (project logos), and `/opt/recvfund/.env`. The `AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in that file decrypts every secret in the database, including hot wallet keys. If it is lost, hot wallets and stored secrets cannot be recovered. Deposit addresses and settlement are not affected, because no deposit keys exist.

## After installing

Open `https://<your-domain>/signup` (or `http://<server-ip>/signup`) and continue with the [Onboarding guide](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/introduction.md). If the server is behind a router or in a virtual machine, the printed address may not open; see [Installing behind a router or in a virtual machine](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/quick-setup.md#installing-behind-a-router-or-in-a-virtual-machine).

To stop the installation without losing data, see [Stopping and starting](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md#stopping-and-starting).


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/quick-setup/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/quick-setup.md

# Quick setup

The installer is a Bash script published as an asset of each [release of recvfund-scripts](https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases); the URL below always serves the newest one. It writes a compose project under `/opt/recvfund`, pulls the newest released version of the public images `ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-api` and `ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-web`, and starts them. Run it on a fresh server over SSH. It needs Bash 4 or newer, `curl` and `openssl`; it installs Docker itself when Docker is missing.

## 1. Run the script

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash
```

The script runs as root through `sudo` so it can install Docker and write `/opt/recvfund`. Pass flags after `-s --`, for example `| sudo bash -s -- --testnet`. Pass `--mainnet` or `--testnet` to skip the menu and the network prompt; see [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md) for every flag.

## 2. Operations menu

With no flags the script shows a menu. Enter `1` for a fresh install.

```
Operations
  1) fresh install
  2) update to the newest release
  3) restart services
  4) reset (remove containers, images and data)
  5) show status
  6) exit
Choice [1]:
```

If `/opt/recvfund/.env` already exists, the script asks whether to update the existing installation, remove it and install again, or cancel.

## 3. System checks and Docker

The script detects the operating system and CPU architecture (amd64 and arm64), checks that `curl` and `openssl` exist, and installs Docker and the compose plugin if they are missing:

```
Docker is not installed. Install it now? [Y/n]:
```

It then creates the install directory, starts writing `/opt/recvfund/install.log`, and checks free disk space. Below 5 GB it asks before continuing; below 10 GB it warns.

## 4. Network

```
Network
  1) mainnet  - real funds
  2) testnet  - Solana devnet and test funds; recommended for a first install
Choice [2]:
```

Testnet is the default and the right choice for a first install. The network type is written to `.env` as `NETWORK_TYPE` and cannot be changed later without `--reset`.

## 5. Database

```
Database
  1) external Postgres - recommended for production
  2) bundled Postgres container - for testing only; data lives in a Docker volume
Choice [2]:
```

With `1`, the script asks for the connection and tests it before going on:

```
Postgres host:
Postgres port [5432]:
Database name [recv]:
Database user [recv]:
Database password:
Connect with SSL? [y/N]:
```

The host must be reachable from inside the `api` container, so `localhost` means the container itself; use the machine's LAN address or, on Docker Desktop, `host.docker.internal`. The bundled database is fine for testnet and for small installs. For mainnet, a managed Postgres with its own backups is the safer choice.

## 6. HTTPS

```
HTTPS
  1) Let's Encrypt - a domain name pointing at this server; ports 80 and 443 must be free
  2) plain HTTP    - by IP address, or behind your own reverse proxy
Choice [2]:
```

With `1`, the script asks:

```
Domain name:
Email for the Let's Encrypt account [admin@<domain>]:
```

It checks that the domain resolves to this server and that ports 80 and 443 are free. Caddy obtains a certificate from Let's Encrypt on the first request and renews it.

With `2`, the script asks:

```
Host port for HTTP [80]:
Public site URL (as reached by browsers; editable later in Settings) [http://<server-ip>]:
```

It checks that the port is free. The site URL is used in payment links and emails; change it later under Settings → Site URL if it is wrong. Let's Encrypt is not offered on macOS, which is supported for local testing only.

### Installing behind a router or in a virtual machine

The suggested site URL uses the public address that `api.ipify.org` reports for this machine. On a cloud server, that's the server's own address. Behind a home or office router, or inside a virtual machine such as Lima, it's the router's address. Browsers can't reach the server there, so the printed signup link doesn't open.

In that case, at the site URL prompt, enter an address your browser can reach:

- **Lima on a Mac:** `http://localhost`. Lima forwards the VM's ports to your Mac.
- **Another virtual machine or a machine on your network:** `http://<its LAN address>`, for example `http://192.168.64.5`.

If you used `--yes` or accepted the default, open that address in your browser and finish signup. Then set the same address under **Installation** → **Site URL**. Payment links and emails use the site URL, so they point to the wrong place until you change it. Customers outside your network can't reach a local address. For real payments, install on a server with a public address or a domain.

## 7. Summary and confirmation

The script generates `AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `ADMIN_API_KEY`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (bundled database only) and `REDIS_PASSWORD`, then prints the configuration:

```
Configuration
  Directory:     /opt/recvfund
  OS:            Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (amd64)
  Network:       testnet
  Database:      bundled container (profile db)
  HTTPS:         Let's Encrypt for pay.example.com (ops@example.com)
  Site URL:      https://pay.example.com
  Images:        ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-api and recvfund-web, version 0.1.2
  Secrets:       generated (written only to /opt/recvfund/.env)

Write the files and start the services? [Y/n]:
```

Press Enter to continue. `--yes` skips this and every earlier prompt, taking the defaults: testnet, bundled Postgres, plain HTTP on port 80.

## 8. What the script does next

1. Writes `/opt/recvfund/.env` (mode 600), `docker-compose.yml` and `Caddyfile`.
2. `docker compose pull` (or builds the images with `--source`).
3. Starts `postgres` (bundled installs) and `redis` and waits for them to be healthy.
4. `docker compose run --rm api node dist/src/db/migrate` (schema and seed data).
5. `docker compose up -d`
6. Polls `/api/v1/health` for up to 90 seconds.
7. Prints the signup URL.

```
recv.fund installed

  Create the root account:  https://pay.example.com/signup
  Configuration:            /opt/recvfund/.env
  Logs:                     cd /opt/recvfund && docker compose -p recvfund logs -f --tail=100 api
  Certificate:              Caddy requests it from Let's Encrypt on the first request; allow a minute.

Back up /opt/recvfund/.env now. AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY in that file decrypts every
secret in the database, including hot wallet keys. If it is lost they
cannot be recovered.
```

If the API never reports healthy, the script exits with a nonzero status and points at the log. Run the logs command above to see why.

## 9. Create the root account

Open the signup URL in a browser and continue with [Root account setup](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/root-account-setup.md). The signup page works only until the first account exists; after that the API rejects further root signups.

If the signup link doesn't open, see [Installing behind a router or in a virtual machine](#installing-behind-a-router-or-in-a-virtual-machine).

## Checking on the install

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund ps
docker compose -p recvfund logs -f --tail=100 api
curl -s http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/health
```

Or run the script with `--status`.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md

# Advanced setup

This page documents what the installer produces so you can reproduce or repair it by hand. The stack runs two application images, `recvfund-api` and `recvfund-web`, which are public on GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-api` and `ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-web`, tags `X.Y.Z` per release, `latest` for the newest release), or built on the server only with the `--source` option.

```
Internet ──► caddy :80/:443 ──┬── /api/*  → api:3001   (the server: API, watchers, sweeps, payouts, webhooks)
                              └── /*      → web:3000   (dashboard and /payments checkout)
                       redis     internal only
                       postgres  internal only, profile "db" (or an external Postgres)
```

## Files on the server

```
/opt/recvfund/
├── .env                       # secrets and connection values, mode 600
├── docker-compose.yml         # the stack below
├── Caddyfile                  # routing and TLS
├── install.log                # appended by every installer run
└── docker-compose.build.yml   # only with --source: build overrides for api and web
```

## docker-compose.yml

```yaml
services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
      - '443:443/udp'
    environment:
      SITE_DOMAIN: ${SITE_DOMAIN}
      ACME_EMAIL: ${ACME_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    depends_on:
      - web
      - api

  api:
    image: ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-api:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: 3001
      NETWORK_TYPE: ${NETWORK_TYPE}
      SITE_URL: ${SITE_URL}
      AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      ADMIN_API_KEY: ${ADMIN_API_KEY}
      SEND_WEBHOOKS: ${SEND_WEBHOOKS:-true}
      POSTGRES_HOST: ${POSTGRES_HOST}
      POSTGRES_PORT: ${POSTGRES_PORT}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_SSL: ${POSTGRES_SSL:-false}
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      REDIS_PORT: 6379
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - api-logs:/repo/apps/api/logs
      - api-uploads:/repo/apps/api/uploads
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'wget', '-qO-', 'http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/health']
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  web:
    image: ghcr.io/recv-fund/recvfund-web:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      # Same origin as the browser: Caddy routes /api/* to the api service.
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: /api/v1
      API_INTERNAL_URL: http://api:3001/api/v1
    depends_on:
      - api

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    profiles: ['db']
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: >
      redis-server --requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD} --appendonly yes
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', '-a', '${REDIS_PASSWORD}', 'ping']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  postgres-data:
  redis-data:
  api-logs:
  api-uploads:
```

The installer accepts amd64 and arm64 hosts. The `postgres` service is behind the `db` profile: it starts only when you pass `--profile db`, which the installer does for a bundled database.

## Caddyfile

```
{
	email {$ACME_EMAIL}
}

{$SITE_DOMAIN} {
	encode zstd gzip

	handle /api/* {
		reverse_proxy api:3001
	}

	handle {
		reverse_proxy web:3000
	}
}
```

When `SITE_DOMAIN` is a hostname, Caddy obtains and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate. When it is `:80`, the stack serves plain HTTP.

## Environment variables

Everything in `.env`. The installer writes all of them; edit by hand only if you know what each value does.

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SITE_DOMAIN` | The hostname Caddy serves, with automatic HTTPS. `:80` for plain HTTP (IP address, or behind your own proxy). |
| `ACME_EMAIL` | Email address given to Let's Encrypt for certificate notices. Empty when `SITE_DOMAIN` is `:80`. |
| `SITE_URL` | The public address of this install: used in payment links, emails and the dashboard. Initial value only; editable later under Settings → Site URL, which is stored in the database. |
| `NETWORK_TYPE` | `mainnet` or `testnet`. Decides which chain rows the API serves. Never change it on a running install. |
| `AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | 64 hex characters. Encrypts every secret in the database, including hot wallet private keys and webhook secrets. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Never change it after first start. Back it up off the server. |
| `ADMIN_API_KEY` | Hex string. Authenticates the two platform-configuration administration endpoints of the API (`x-api-key` header). The installer generates it but does not use it. Not a project API key. |
| `POSTGRES_HOST` | `postgres` for the bundled container; a hostname for an external server. |
| `POSTGRES_PORT` | Default `5432`. |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | Default `recv`. |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Generated by the installer for the bundled database. |
| `POSTGRES_DB` | Default `recv`. |
| `POSTGRES_SSL` | `true` or `false`. Use `true` for most managed Postgres services. |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | Generated by the installer. Redis is only reachable inside the compose network. It holds caches and rate-limit counters; queues and job state are in Postgres. |
| `SEND_WEBHOOKS` | `true` by default. `false` stops every webhook delivery server-wide. Useful on a staging copy of a production database. |
| `IMAGE_TAG` | Image version to run. The installer writes the newest released version (for example `0.1.2`); `--image-tag` overrides it. `--update` changes it. |

Every other setting (sweep triggers, payment expiry, rate limits, SMTP, site URL) lives in the database and is edited in the dashboard, not in `.env`.

A complete example for a bundled database and plain HTTP:

```
SITE_DOMAIN=:80
ACME_EMAIL=
SITE_URL=http://203.0.113.10
NETWORK_TYPE=testnet
AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<64 hex characters>
ADMIN_API_KEY=<hex>
POSTGRES_HOST=postgres
POSTGRES_PORT=5432
POSTGRES_USER=recv
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<generated>
POSTGRES_DB=recv
POSTGRES_SSL=false
REDIS_PASSWORD=<generated>
SEND_WEBHOOKS=true
IMAGE_TAG=0.1.2
```

## Volumes

| Volume | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `postgres-data` | The bundled database. Not used with an external Postgres. |
| `redis-data` | Redis append-only file. Safe to lose; caches and rate-limit counters rebuild. |
| `caddy-data` | Certificates and ACME account. Losing it means a new certificate request on next start. |
| `caddy-config` | Caddy's runtime config. |
| `api-logs` | API log files. |
| `api-uploads` | Uploaded project logos. Back it up with the database. Replacing the API container keeps it. |

## Starting by hand

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db pull
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db up -d --wait postgres redis
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db run --rm api node dist/src/db/migrate
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db up -d --remove-orphans
curl -s http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/health
```

Leave out `--profile db`, and start only `redis` in the second command, when `POSTGRES_HOST` points at an external server. With `--source`, add `-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.build.yml` and replace `pull` with `build --pull`.

The API refuses to start with unapplied migrations, which is why `migrate` runs first.

## External Postgres

Point `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_PORT`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB` and `POSTGRES_SSL` at a Postgres 16 server, and start the stack without `--profile db`. The user needs to own the database: migrations create the `recv` and `recv_ops` schemas and their tables. Allow the server's IP in the database firewall.

The installer sets this up when you choose `external` at the database prompt, or pass `--external-db` with the `--pg-*` options. It tests the connection before writing any file.

## Behind your own proxy

If another proxy or load balancer already owns ports 80 and 443, run the stack on plain HTTP on a different host port and forward to it.

1. Set `SITE_DOMAIN=:80` and `ACME_EMAIL=` in `.env`.
2. Change the `caddy` port mapping to your chosen port, for example `'8080:80'`, and remove the `443` mappings.
3. Set `SITE_URL` to the public HTTPS address your proxy serves.
4. Forward that address to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` on the server, passing the `Host` header through.

The installer does steps 1 to 3 for you with `--http-port 8080 --site-url https://pay.example.com`. Add `--http-bind 127.0.0.1` when the proxy runs on the same server, so port 8080 isn't reachable from outside. Without `--site-url`, it asks for the site URL (with `--yes`, it uses `http://<server-ip>:8080`). The dashboard shows the site URL under Settings → Site URL; correct it there so payment links and emails carry the address your proxy serves.

## Updating by hand

`--update` does the following; run it yourself if you prefer.

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db pull
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db up -d --wait postgres redis
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db run --rm api node dist/src/db/migrate
docker compose -p recvfund --env-file .env --profile db up -d --remove-orphans
```

To pin a version, set `IMAGE_TAG` in `.env` before pulling. Keep `.env` otherwise identical across updates: a changed `AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or `NETWORK_TYPE` makes existing data unreadable or mismatched.

## Backups

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund exec postgres pg_dump -U recv recv > backup.sql
docker run --rm -v recvfund_api-uploads:/uploads -v "$PWD":/backup alpine tar czf /backup/uploads.tgz -C /uploads .
cp .env env.backup
```

Restore is the reverse: restore the dump into an empty database, restore the uploads archive into the `api-uploads` volume, put `.env` back, start the stack. With an external Postgres, use that service's own backups and still keep a copy of `.env`.

## Stopping and starting

The installer has no stop operation. Stop and start the containers with Docker Compose from the install directory. Run the commands with `sudo` if your user isn't in the `docker` group. Leave out `--profile db` when you use an external Postgres.

To stop every container and keep all data:

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund --profile db stop
```

To start the stopped containers again:

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund --profile db start
```

`down` removes the containers but keeps the volumes, `.env` and the database. Bring the stack back with `up -d`:

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund --profile db down
docker compose -p recvfund --profile db up -d
```

Without `--profile db`, these commands skip the bundled Postgres container, so `stop` leaves it running. Every container has `restart: unless-stopped`. A container you stopped stays stopped after a reboot, and one you didn't stop starts again with Docker.

{/* prettier-ignore */}
> [!CAUTION]
>
> Don't add `-v` to `down`. It deletes the volumes, including the bundled
> database. `--reset` also deletes everything; see
> [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md).

## Day-two commands

```bash
cd /opt/recvfund
docker compose -p recvfund ps
docker compose -p recvfund logs -f --tail=100 api
docker compose -p recvfund restart api
curl -s http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/health
```


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md

# Script usage

The install script handles installs, updates, restarts, status checks and resets. The newest release is always served at the URL below; a specific release is at `https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/install.sh`, next to a `SHA256SUMS` file:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- [operation] [options]
```

Flags go after `-s --`. The script finds the newest released version by reading the image tags on `ghcr.io`; if it can't reach the registry, it stops and asks for `--image-tag`. With no operation flag the script shows an operations menu. `--help` prints the same reference as this page; `--version` prints the script version.

## Common commands

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --testnet     # first install, test networks
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --mainnet     # production install
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --update      # move to this release's images, migrate, restart
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --restart     # restart without touching data
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --status      # container status and health
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --reset       # remove everything (confirm twice)
```

`https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/update.sh` is a shortcut for `install.sh --update` and accepts the same options.

## Operations

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--mainnet` | Fresh install against Solana mainnet and Robinhood Chain mainnet. Sets `NETWORK_TYPE=mainnet`. |
| `--testnet` | Fresh install against Solana devnet and Robinhood Chain testnet. Sets `NETWORK_TYPE=testnet`. Every payment is a test payment. |
| `--update` | Set `IMAGE_TAG` to the newest released version (or to `--image-tag`), pull those images (or rebuild from `--source`), run migrations against the new image, then replace the containers. Data and the rest of `.env` are untouched. The script prints the version it moves from and to, or says the installation is already on the newest release. It refuses to move a newer installed version back to an older one unless `--image-tag` is given. |
| `--restart` | Restart every container without pulling or changing data. Use it when the dashboard reports that blocks are no longer being processed. |
| `--status` | Print `docker compose ps` for the project and the response of `/api/v1/health`. |
| `--reset` | Stop and remove the containers, the images, every volume (including the bundled database) and the install directory. You must type the install directory path twice to confirm. Cannot be undone. Back up `.env` and the database first. |

There's no stop operation. To stop the containers and keep the data, see [Stopping and starting](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md#stopping-and-starting).

Without an operation flag, the script shows the menu. If an installation already exists in the directory, a fresh install asks whether to update it, remove it and install again, or cancel.

## Options

| Flag | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Accept the default answer for every prompt. Combine with the options below for an unattended install. | prompt |
| `--domain <host>` | Hostname that points at this server. Caddy obtains a Let's Encrypt certificate for it. Sets `SITE_DOMAIN` and `SITE_URL=https://<host>`. Requires ports 80 and 443 and cannot be combined with `--http-port`. | prompt; default is plain HTTP |
| `--email <address>` | Email address for the Let's Encrypt account. Sets `ACME_EMAIL`. Only used with a domain. | `admin@<domain>` |
| `--external-db` | Use an existing Postgres 16 server instead of the bundled container. Prompts for the connection unless the `--pg-*` options are given. The stack then starts without the `db` profile. | bundled Postgres |
| `--pg-host <host>` | External Postgres host, as reachable from inside the `api` container. Implies `--external-db`. | prompt |
| `--pg-port <port>` | External Postgres port. | `5432` |
| `--pg-db <name>` | External Postgres database name. | `recv` |
| `--pg-user <user>` | External Postgres user. | `recv` |
| `--pg-password <pw>` | External Postgres password. Visible in the process list while the script runs; prefer the prompt. | prompt, hidden |
| `--pg-ssl` | Connect to the external Postgres with SSL. | prompt, default no |
| `--http-port <n>` | Serve plain HTTP on that host port instead of 80 and 443, for a server where your own proxy terminates TLS. Sets `SITE_DOMAIN=:80` and maps the port. The site URL defaults to `http://<server-ip>:<n>`; set the public address under Settings → Site URL afterwards. | 80 and 443, or the HTTP port prompt |
| `--http-bind <ip>` | Publish the HTTP port on this IPv4 address only, for example `127.0.0.1` when your proxy runs on the same server. Without it, the port is open on every address of the server, and Docker's port publishing is not blocked by `ufw`. Plain HTTP only. | every address |
| `--site-url <url>` | The public address of the installation in plain-HTTP mode, for example `https://pay.example.com` when your proxy serves HTTPS. Skips the site URL prompt. | prompt; suggests `http://<public ip>[:port]` |
| `--image-tag <tag>` | Image version to run instead of the newest release, for example `0.1.2`. Written to `.env` as `IMAGE_TAG`. | the newest released version |
| `--dir <path>` | Install directory. Must be an absolute path. | `/opt/recvfund` |
| `--source <path>` | Build the API and web images from a source checkout at `<path>` instead of pulling them. Writes `docker-compose.build.yml`, which later updates reuse. Only for people with source access. | pull images |

Options can also be written as `--flag=value`.

Environment variables: `RECV_DRY_RUN=1` prints the Docker commands instead of running them; `NO_COLOR=1` disables coloured output.

## Examples

Unattended testnet install on an IP address, plain HTTP on port 80:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --testnet --yes
```

Mainnet with a domain, Let's Encrypt and a managed database:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --mainnet \
  --domain pay.example.com --email ops@example.com \
  --pg-host db.example.com --pg-db recv --pg-user recv --pg-ssl
```

The database password is asked for at the prompt. Add `--yes` and `--pg-password` only where a password in the process list is acceptable.

Behind your own proxy on the same server, port 8080 reachable from that proxy only:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --mainnet --yes \
  --http-port 8080 --http-bind 127.0.0.1 --site-url https://pay.example.com
```

Pin a version and update to it later:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --update --image-tag 1.0.2
```

## What the script writes

```
/opt/recvfund/.env                       mode 600; AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY is the value to back up
/opt/recvfund/docker-compose.yml
/opt/recvfund/Caddyfile
/opt/recvfund/install.log                every run appends to it
/opt/recvfund/docker-compose.build.yml   only with --source
```

See [Advanced setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md) for the contents of each file.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/payment-links/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/payment-links.md

# Payment links

A payment is a request for a USD amount from one customer of one project. It has a reference UUID and a checkout URL. The customer opens the URL and pays with a wallet or by sending to a deposit address. Your server watches the chain, credits the payment and sends a webhook when its state changes.

## Creating a payment

**From the dashboard.** Open **Payments** and use **Create payment link**. Pick a customer with **Find customer** (search by email or customer ID); a full email address that matches no customer offers **Create customer**, which creates and selects it, enter **Amount (USD)** and optionally an **Invoice ID**. The link is shown after saving. Owners, admins and project leads can create links. Creation needs an active project, an active customer in that project, and a configured site URL (Installation → Site URL).

**From the API.** `POST /api/v1/payment` with the project's `API-Key` header creates the customer if needed and returns `reference_id` and the checkout `url`. See [Create payment](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/create-payment.md).

Both paths share the same validation. A payment carries:

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Amount | USD, positive, at most 18 integer and 6 fractional digits. Stored and returned as a decimal string. |
| Customer | A customer of the same project. Customer IDs are unique within a project. |
| Project | The project the link or key belongs to. |
| Invoice ID | Optional label, echoed in webhooks as `invoice_id`. Not unique and not an idempotency key. |
| Reference | A version 4 UUID that identifies the payment everywhere. |
| Expiry | Default `payment.expiryHours` (24 hours, configurable from 1 to 8760). The API accepts an explicit future timestamp with a timezone instead. |
| Currency and network | Optional API restriction to one currency code and one chain (`SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`). |
| Source | `dashboard-link` or `api`. |

The checkout URL is `{site URL}/payments?reference_id={uuid}`. Testnet installs add `&test=true`.

## States

The dashboard shows the database names. The API and webhooks use the same states in upper case.

| Dashboard | API | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `OPEN` | Created, no confirmed funds yet. |
| `partially-filled` | `PARTIALLY_FILLED` | Confirmed funds below the requested amount. |
| `filled` | `FILLED` | Confirmed funds within `payment.fillToleranceUsd` (default 0.01 USD) of the requested amount. |
| `over-filled` | `OVER_FILLED` | Confirmed funds above the requested amount plus the tolerance. |
| `cancelled` | `CANCELLED` | Cancelled from the dashboard, or expired. |

Transitions:

- `open` becomes `filled`, `partially-filled` or `over-filled` when the confirmed USD total is compared with the requested amount.
- `partially-filled` becomes `filled` or `over-filled` when a later deposit is confirmed. A partially filled payment does not expire and keeps accepting deposits after its original expiry.
- `open` becomes `cancelled` when you cancel it or when it passes its expiry. A scheduler runs every minute and cancels up to 500 expired open payments per pass.
- Funds confirmed after cancellation still move the payment to `filled`, `partially-filled` or `over-filled`. The cancellation time is kept as history. Received funds are always recorded.

Only an `open` payment can be cancelled. If two people cancel at the same time, one succeeds and the other gets a conflict.

## Confirmations and valuation

A transfer is recorded as `detected` when it is found, and contributes no USD until it reaches the chain's confirmation threshold. The confirmation worker rechecks detected transfers every `watcher.confirmationsIntervalSeconds` (default 15 seconds) while `watcher.enabled` is true. Each new confirmation count sends a `payment.confirming` webhook. On Solana a finalized transaction counts as the configured threshold. On Robinhood Chain the receipt must belong to the canonical block when it is read.

The USD value of a transfer is the gross on-chain amount at the price fetched on first detection, rounded down to six places. That price is kept across rechecks. Stablecoins are priced at exactly 1.00 by policy. SOL and ETH use a fresh CoinGecko quote; if no fresh price is available the transfer waits and is not credited with a guessed value.

Every transfer that credits a payment is a transfer to the customer's deposit address, recorded with kind `deposit`, whether the customer paid from a connected wallet on the checkout page or sent the funds from any other wallet or exchange. The full amount arrives at the deposit address; the recv.fund fee is taken later, at [sweep](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md). See [Customer deposit wallets](https://docs.recv.fund/features/customer-deposit-wallets.md) for how a deposit is matched to a payment.

## The checkout page

The public page `/payments?reference_id=...` uses its own layout and no dashboard session. It loads the payment, the project name, logo and brand colour, and the currencies enabled for the project whose chain has an active merchant registration. It polls the payment status every five seconds. Testnet payments carry a **Testnet** label.

1. Under **Pay with** the customer chooses a currency and network. Options show why they are unavailable when they are.
2. Selecting a currency assigns the customer's permanent deposit address on that chain and creates a quote: the exact token amount for the remaining USD, computed by dividing in base units and rounding up once. A quote lasts `payment.quoteTtlSeconds` (default 300 seconds, 30 to 3600) and is cut short by the payment's expiry or the price's freshness deadline. Stablecoin quotes use the fixed price.
3. The page shows the converted amount, the **Deposit address** and a QR code containing the address. The customer can send from any wallet or exchange. The QR encodes the destination; the customer must use the shown currency and network.
4. With an injected browser wallet (EVM or Solana), **Wallet steps** builds one transaction for the connected wallet: a plain transfer of the quoted amount to the customer's deposit address. On Robinhood Chain it is an ERC-20 `transfer` or an ETH transfer, with no approval step. On Solana it is a SOL transfer, or for an SPL token an instruction that creates the deposit token account if it is missing (paid by the customer) followed by the token transfer. Every currency can be paid this way, SOL included. No recv.fund contract or program instruction runs. WalletConnect is not available in this release; only injected wallets are supported.
5. After the wallet sends the transaction, the browser submits its hash to the server, which reads the transaction from the chain and verifies that it contains a transfer of the selected currency to the customer's deposit address before recording anything. The page shows "Transaction submitted. Payment status updates after network verification." No browser claim marks a payment paid. If the browser closes before submitting the hash, the deposit watcher finds the transfer like any other deposit.

The currency cannot be changed once any transfer has been recorded. A closed, expired or unavailable payment cannot be quoted or prepared for wallet payment. The checkout progress stages are `waiting`, `sent`, `confirming`, `complete` and `cancelled`. A project's custom CSS is stored but not applied to the checkout page in this release. The endpoints behind the page are documented under [Checkout endpoints](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/checkout-endpoints.md).

## Partial and over payment

The credited total is the sum of all confirmed transfers, in every currency the customer used. A total below the requested amount leaves the payment `partially-filled`; a later deposit can complete it. A total above the requested amount plus the tolerance makes it `over-filled`. The excess is recorded on the payment and in the customer's history. There is no refund function in this release; if you want to return the excess, create a [payout](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md).

## History and details

**Payment history** on the Payments page lists the current project's payments, or all accessible projects. Filters: text search over invoice ID, reference and customer, status, webhook status, chain and currency, source, and inclusive created-date bounds, with sorting and pagination. The summary line counts open (including partially filled), closed (filled and over-filled) and cancelled payments.

**Payment details** shows the state, expiry, checkout link, the latest 100 transactions with their hashes, and the latest 100 webhook deliveries with attempts and results. **Cancel payment** is available while the payment is `open`.

## CSV export

**Export CSV** downloads the rows matching the current filters. Exports are capped at 10,000 rows; narrow the filters if the cap is reached. Values that a spreadsheet would read as a formula are neutralised. All roles that can read payments, including project managers, can export.

## Related

- [Payment status](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status.md) for reading a payment from the API.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md) for the events sent on each transition.
- [Take a test payment](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/test-payment.md).


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/customer-deposit-wallets/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/customer-deposit-wallets.md

# Customer deposit wallets

Every customer of a project gets one permanent deposit address per chain. Every payment the customer makes goes to it: a wallet payment from the checkout page is a transfer to this address, and the customer can also send any amount to it from any wallet or exchange, at any time. Your server watches the address, credits the funds to a payment, and [sweeps](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md) the balance to your settlement wallet. No fee is taken when funds arrive.

## Addresses are derived, not generated

The address is computed from your merchant registration and the customer's random reference. No private key for it exists anywhere.

| Chain | Derivation | Where tokens go |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solana | A program-derived address (PDA) with seeds `deposit`, your merchant account and the customer reference. | SPL tokens go to the mint's associated token account (ATA) owned by that PDA. The PDA itself receives SOL. |
| Robinhood Chain | A CREATE2 address computed by your merchant contract (`MerchantVault`) from the customer reference. | Tokens and ETH go to that address. It is valid before anything is deployed there; your merchant contract deploys a forwarder contract at the address on its first sweep. |

Funds at a deposit address can move only to your registered settlement wallet and to the fee collector recorded in your registration, and only through a sweep. Deactivating your registration does not block sweeps. On Robinhood Chain the server can derive deposit addresses only after your merchant contract exists, that is, after the registration is confirmed.

An address is assigned the first time the customer selects that chain on the checkout page, or when your system calls [Assign deposit address](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address.md). Assignment requires an active customer, project and merchant registration on that chain; the server checks the live registration state before storing the address. The same address is reused for every later payment by that customer on that chain. Assignment is not a dashboard action. On Solana the API returns the PDA; the receiving address for an SPL token is the currency-specific `customerAddress` from [Deposit options](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md).

## The Customers page

**Customers** lists the current project's customers with **Requested** (the sum of their payment amounts), **Received** (the sum of confirmed transfers, including unmatched deposits) and their deposit addresses. Search by email or customer ID.

**Create customer** takes an email and an optional **Customer ID**. Use your own ID to connect the record to your application, or leave it blank and recv.fund generates `cust_` followed by 12 hex characters. IDs are unique within a project; a duplicate returns a conflict. Owners, admins and project leads can create customers; other roles read.

**Customer details** shows each deposit address with its chain, status (`active`, `dormant` or `inactive`) and **Deposit scan**: the time of the last automatic scan, or the current error for an asset on that address, so an RPC problem is visible. It also lists the latest 100 payments and the latest 100 transactions, with full counts.

## How deposits are found

The deposit watcher runs every `watcher.depositsIntervalSeconds` (default 15 seconds) while `watcher.enabled` is true. Each pass visits the 20 least recently scanned addresses and one currency per address, so a large address set is covered over several passes. Progress per address and currency is stored, and a page is only marked complete after every transfer on it has been verified and recorded, so a restart replays safely.

- On Robinhood Chain, scanning starts at the block height recorded when the address was assigned. ERC-20 scans read `Transfer` logs in chunks of `watcher.evmLogBlockChunk` blocks (default 2000). Native ETH scans need an RPC node that supports `debug_traceTransaction` and `debug_traceBlockByHash` with the call tracer, and read at most 64 blocks per page.
- On Solana, scanning pages the signature history of the PDA or the token account, `watcher.solanaSignatureBatch` signatures at a time (default 200).

RPC nodes must retain the history needed to catch up. See [Node configuration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/node-configuration.md).

## How a deposit is credited

A transfer is credited only from proof read from the chain: the server re-derives the address, verifies the transaction and reads the transferred amount. A balance increase, or an amount reported by a browser, never creates a credit.

`payment.unmatchedDepositPolicy` decides which payment receives it:

| Policy | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `credit-latest-open` (default) | The transfer goes to an eligible payment (`open` and unexpired, or `partially-filled`). The server first looks for one whose current quote has the transfer's currency and exact amount, which is the payment a wallet checkout paid even if the watcher sees the transfer before the page confirms it; otherwise it takes the customer's newest eligible payment. If the payment restricts the chain or currency, the transfer must match. The first matched transfer sets the payment's currency, chain and deposit address, so the customer does not have to open the checkout page before sending. |
| `leave-unmatched` | Every deposit is recorded without a payment. |

`filled`, `over-filled` and `cancelled` payments never receive new matches. When no eligible payment exists, the transfer is stored as an unmatched deposit: it has no payment, stays visible in the customer's history through its deposit address, counts in the customer's **Received** total and in [Analytics](https://docs.recv.fund/features/analytics.md), and is swept like any other balance. The binding is fixed at first detection: replaying an old unmatched transfer never pays a payment created later, and a transfer matched before its payment was cancelled still credits that payment.

Deposits follow the confirmation and valuation rules in [Payment links](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payment-links.md#confirmations-and-valuation). The transfer's fee is recorded as null because the fee is taken at sweep time.

A wallet payment from the checkout page is a deposit like any other, with one difference: when the page submits its hash and the server records the transfer for the first time, the transfer is credited to the payment that was being paid, whatever other payments are open. If the deposit watcher recorded the transfer first, the watcher's match is kept, and the checkout confirmation returns a conflict when that match is not the payment being paid. A transfer in any supported currency is recorded even if that currency has since been disabled for the project.

## Missed-payment reports

If a customer sent funds and nothing was credited, report the transaction under **Missed payments**. Choose the network, paste the **Transaction hash or signature** and an optional note (up to 2000 characters). Owners, admins and project leads can submit; project managers can read. A project can have at most 100 open reports; resubmitting the same hash returns the existing report.

A worker checks the ten least recently checked open reports per pass, on the same interval and switch as confirmations. For each report it:

1. Verifies the transaction and its confirmation depth. Unknown or unconfirmed transactions, and RPC nodes without the history, leave the report `open` with a retry message. A confirmed failed transaction makes it `rejected`.
2. Rechecks the customer's addresses and currencies against the transaction, ten address and currency pairs per pass, ignoring the automatic scan's starting height. This recovers a transfer sent before the address was assigned, or to an address or currency that was inactive.

A confirmed transfer recorded for the project makes the report `credited`, including a deposit kept without a payment. A confirmed transaction with a complete, error-free scan and no matching transfer is `rejected`; add the missing address or currency and resubmit, which reopens the report. Open rows on the page refresh every ten seconds.

## Not in this release

Reconciliation after a deep chain reorganisation is not implemented. Confirmed transfers are treated as final once they reach the chain's confirmation threshold.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/multi-brand-projects/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/multi-brand-projects.md

# Projects

A project is one brand or store inside your install. Customers, payments, deposit addresses, payouts, API keys and webhook endpoints all belong to a project. The first project is created with the root account at setup. Owners and admins can create more under **Projects**.

## Project switcher

The dashboard shell has a project selector. List pages show the selected project, or all projects you can see. Owners and admins see every project; other roles see the projects they were assigned in [User management](https://docs.recv.fund/features/user-management.md). The server checks project membership on every request independently of what the UI shows.

## What is configured per project

### Branding

Shown on the project's checkout page.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The merchant name the customer sees. |
| Website URL, Success redirect URL, Cancel redirect URL | HTTP(S) URLs. The redirect URLs are returned to the checkout page with the payment. |
| Brand colour | Six-digit hex colour. |
| Logo | PNG, JPEG or SVG up to 512 KB. The upload is decoded, converted to PNG and resized to fit 512 by 512. SVG files containing scripts, external references, entities or embedded HTML are rejected. The original file is never served. Logos are stored in the `api-uploads` volume; back it up with the database. |
| Custom CSS | Stored, up to 32 KiB. Not applied to the checkout page in this release. |

Owners, admins and project leads can edit branding.

### Enabled currencies

**Enabled currencies** lists every active currency on the active chains of your install's network (mainnet or testnet), for example USDC, USDT and SOL on Solana and USDG and ETH on Robinhood Chain. Tick the ones this project accepts. The checkout page and the API's deposit options show only enabled currencies whose chain has an active merchant registration for the project. Enabling a currency that is inactive or on another network fails. See [Networks](https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks.md).

### Withdrawal policy

Limits for [payouts](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md), evaluated in USD:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum (USD) | Overrides the install-wide minimum (`payout.minimumUsd`, default 1). Blank inherits it. The effective minimum is shown above the form. |
| Automatic approval maximum (USD) | Ceiling for automatic approval of API payouts. |
| Daily limit per recipient (USD) | Rolling 24-hour limit per recipient email. Blank removes the cap. |
| Hourly limit per recipient (USD) | Rolling one-hour limit per recipient email. Blank removes the cap. |
| Allow automatic API payout approval up to the configured maximum | When ticked, API payouts at or below the maximum skip administrator approval. Requires a positive maximum. Dashboard payouts always need approval. |

Only owners and admins change the withdrawal policy.

### Developers

API keys and webhook endpoints are created per project on the **Developers** page. A key authenticates only its own project's payments and payouts; an endpoint receives only its own project's events. See [API keys](https://docs.recv.fund/features/api-keys.md) and [Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md).

### Wallets and registration

Each project has one hot wallet assignment per chain family (Solana, EVM) and one on-chain merchant registration per chain with its own settlement wallet. See [Hot wallet](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/hot-wallet.md) and [Merchant registration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/merchant-registration.md).

### Sweep settings

Each project can override the install's sweep thresholds or use the defaults. See [Sweeps](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md).

### Address book

Saved payout destinations are per project. The same address can be saved in another project independently.

## Roles inside a project

| Action | Roles |
| --- | --- |
| Create a project, deactivate it, change its withdrawal policy | owner, admin |
| Edit branding, logo, enabled currencies, API keys, webhook endpoints | owner, admin, project-lead (in their projects) |
| Read project settings | any member |

Every mutation locks the project and rechecks the acting user and their membership inside the same transaction, so a role change takes effect immediately.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/api-keys/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/api-keys.md

# API keys

Your own systems call the recv.fund API on your server with a project API key. The key identifies the project; every request is scoped to it. Keys are managed on the **Developers** page by owners, admins and project leads.

## Creating a key

**Create API key** takes a **Key name**, for example `Production integration`. The key is 32 hexadecimal characters (16 random bytes). It is shown once, on creation; copy it then. The server stores only a SHA-256 hash and a short prefix, so a lost key cannot be recovered. Create a new one instead.

The **API keys** table shows Name, Prefix and Status. Each row has:

- **Deactivate** / **Activate**: an inactive key is refused with the same `401` as an invalid key. Reactivating restores it.
- **Delete**: removes the key. Applications using it lose access. The activity log keeps the key's past entries.

Revocation is immediate. There is no positive authentication cache, and every write rechecks the key inside its transaction, so a key deactivated while a request is in flight cannot complete a write.

## Using a key

Send the key in the `API-Key` header with `Content-Type: application/json`:

```
API-Key: 811b12035f0dfa8ffd62296df3c98b27
```

The keyed routes are:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/payment` | [Create payment](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/create-payment.md) |
| `GET /api/v1/blockchain-currency/reference/{reference_id}` | [Deposit options](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md) |
| `POST /api/v1/deposit-address/reference/{reference_id}` | [Assign deposit address](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address.md) |
| `GET /api/v1/payment/reference/{reference_id}` | [Payment status](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status.md) |
| `POST /api/v1/withdrawal/merchant`, `GET /api/v1/withdrawal/merchant`, `GET /api/v1/withdrawal/{id}/merchant` | [Payouts API](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payouts-api.md) |

The [checkout endpoints](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/checkout-endpoints.md) need no key.

## Scope

- A key reads and writes only its project. A payment or payout of another project returns `404`.
- An inactive project makes all of its keys return `401`.
- A key never grants dashboard access, and a dashboard session never substitutes for a key.
- The dashboard API and the keyed API are separate surfaces; see [API integration](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/introduction.md).

The activity log records the key ID and project for keyed writes and denied reads, never the key itself.

## Rate limit

`rateLimit.publicApi.perMinute` (default 300, 1 to 10000) limits requests per key per minute, counted across all keyed routes. Exceeding it returns `429` with code `RATE_LIMITED`. The counter lives in Redis; if Redis is unavailable the keyed routes return `503` rather than allowing unlimited requests. The checkout endpoints have a separate per-IP limit, `rateLimit.checkout.perMinute` (default 120).

## Not a project key

`ADMIN_API_KEY` in `.env` is a different credential. It authenticates the two platform-configuration administration endpoints of the API through an `x-api-key` header and is not accepted on the routes above. See [Advanced setup](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md).


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/user-management/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/user-management.md

# User management

Access to the dashboard is by email and password. Every account has one role and, for project roles, a list of assigned projects. The root account created at setup is the only owner.

## Roles

| Role | Dashboard label | What it can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | (not assignable) | Everything. Only the owner changes the site URL and the install-wide minimum payout. Cannot be removed or deactivated. |
| `admin` | Admin | Everything across all projects: projects and withdrawal policy, nodes, installation settings, hot wallets, team, activity log, payout approval. Cannot change or remove themselves, and cannot create another owner. |
| `project-lead` | Project lead | In assigned projects: branding, currencies, API keys, webhook endpoints, hot wallet assignment, merchant registration, customers, payment links, missed-payment reports, sweeps, payout requests and the address book. Can list the project team and invite project managers and project operators into those projects. |
| `project-manager` | Project manager | Read-only in assigned projects, plus CSV export. |
| `project-ops` | Project operator | Reads payments, customers and sweeps of assigned projects. No access to payouts or the address book. |

Anything not allowed for a role returns `403`, whether or not the control is visible. Owner-only settings are shown read-only to other roles. The navigation hides Payouts and Address book for project operators, and shows Hot wallets, Developers and Team only to owners, admins and project leads. Nodes and Activity are owner and admin only.

## Inviting a member

Owners and admins invite from **Team** with **Invite a team member**: Full name, Email address, Role, **Temporary password** and the **Projects** to assign. Project leads can invite only project managers and project operators, and only into their own projects.

The account exists immediately. No email is sent; share the temporary password with the person separately. Until they change it, the account can do nothing except read its own profile and change its password: the dashboard sends them to the change-password page and does not open the shell. Changing the password checks the current password and the confirmation, then signs out every session, so they sign in again with the new password. Passwords must be at least `auth.password.minLength` characters (default 10).

## Changing, deactivating and removing

Owners and admins can change a member's role and project assignments, deactivate or reactivate them, and remove them. Every one of these changes signs the member out on every device. A deactivated account is refused at sign-in and on every request. **Remove** asks for confirmation, deletes the account and its project access, keeps configuration values the person created, and clears their name from those records. The owner cannot be removed.

## Sessions

Sign-in issues an access token (`auth.accessToken.expiresIn`, default 15 minutes) and a refresh token (`auth.refreshToken.expiresIn`, default 30 days). Refresh replaces the old token; reusing a consumed refresh token revokes the whole session family. Sign-out revokes the family. A password change, a role or project change, and deactivation revoke all of the account's sessions. Every request loads the account from the database, so a revocation takes effect on the next request.

Sign-in is rate limited by `rateLimit.login.perHour` (default 20) per IP address and per email address. If the rate limiter is unavailable, sign-in returns `503` rather than skipping the limit.

## Profile

**My account** lets each member edit their full name and username, open the password change page and sign out.

## Activity log

**Activity** (owners and admins) lists what the API recorded: every write request and every denied request, including requests blocked by a role or project check. Successful reads are not recorded. Filter by **Category** and **Outcome** (Success, Denied, Error). Each row shows the time, event, user and details: the path without its query string, HTTP status, duration, the project when known and the request payload with credentials, secrets and URLs redacted. The API records rows after sending the response and finishes pending rows on shutdown. This is an activity log for operating the install, not a transactional compliance ledger.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/analytics/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/analytics.md

# Analytics

**Overview** is the first page of the dashboard. It reports what has been received, from stored ledger values. It makes no RPC or price requests, so it does not show current balances.

## What is counted

- Every confirmed transfer to a deposit address, whether paid from a connected wallet on the checkout page or sent from elsewhere, including deposits that were not matched to a payment. Transfers still waiting for confirmations, and orphaned transfers, are excluded.
- The gross incoming amount at the USD price stored when the transfer was first detected. Stablecoins are 1.00. The figures are receipts, not settlement proceeds, sweep results, payout totals or current market value.
- Receipts stay visible after a project, chain or currency is deactivated.

A payer is a customer, identified through the payment or the deposit address. A customer counts once per period and once in each chart bucket where it paid. A first-time payer's first confirmed receipt falls inside the bucket and inside the selected period; every other active payer in the bucket is returning. Customer identity is per project: the same external customer ID in two projects is two payers. Receipts whose customer was deleted still add USD but do not count as a payer.

## Scope and filters

The page follows the project selector: one project, or every project you can see. Every role can read the projects it is assigned to.

**Date range** presets: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month, Last 3 months, Last 6 months, All time, and Custom dates with **From date** and **Through date** (inclusive). All dates are UTC regardless of the server or browser time zone. Today, the rolling presets and month-to-date include the current UTC day. All time starts at the first confirmed receipt. Reversed or future ranges are rejected.

**Group by** switches the second chart and the distribution between **Network** and **Currency**. Currency groups distinguish the same ticker on different chains.

**Refresh** reloads the current filters. Changing the project resets the view.

## What the page shows

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| KPI cards | All-time receipts in USD; receipts in the range with the change against the previous period; paying customers all time and in the range; customers with at least one payment request all time, and new paying customers in the range. |
| Receipts by project | One series per selected project, including projects with no activity, with an exact table by date. |
| Receipts by network or currency | One series per group, with an exact table. |
| Receipt distribution | USD, token units and share per group. Token units are shown only when the group is one currency; a mixed network group shows none. Shares are rounded to two decimals. |
| Paying customer activity | First-time and returning payers per bucket, with totals. |
| Recent confirmed transfers | The latest ten confirmed receipts in the range, with confirmation time, transaction and source. |

The comparison period immediately precedes the selected range and has the same number of UTC days. Percentage change is (current minus previous) divided by previous, as a two-decimal string; a zero baseline with activity shows no percentage. Ranges up to 366 days use daily buckets, longer ranges monthly buckets, and ranges over 100 years yearly buckets. Empty dates are zero-filled. Amounts are exact decimal strings from the database to the browser; they are never converted to floating point.

For the full payment ledger use [payment history and CSV export](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payment-links.md#history-and-details).


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md

# Payouts

A payout sends a token amount from a project's hot wallet to an address. It is a direct transfer signed by the hot wallet; it does not go through the recv.fund program and does not need a merchant registration. Payouts are created in the dashboard or through the [Payouts API](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payouts-api.md), approved by an administrator with an emailed one-time code, and then signed, sent and confirmed by a worker on your server.

## Before the first payout

- Configure SMTP under Installation → **Email delivery** and send a **Test email**. Approval codes are sent by email; without SMTP, approval fails.
- Assign an active hot wallet to the project for the chain's family, holding the token to send and the native currency for fees. See [Hot wallet](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/hot-wallet.md).
- Set the project's [withdrawal policy](https://docs.recv.fund/features/multi-brand-projects.md#withdrawal-policy) if the install defaults do not fit.

## Address book

**Address book** stores payout destinations per project: **Recipient name**, **Recipient email**, chain, **Destination address** and optional notes (up to 2000 characters). The address is validated and canonicalised for the chain without an RPC call; the EVM zero address is rejected. A destination can be saved once per project and chain; save a separate recipient for another chain, because the chain of a saved recipient cannot be changed. A project can hold up to 10,000 recipients.

Owners, admins and project leads add, edit and remove recipients in a selected project. Project managers read. Project operators have no access. Removal asks for confirmation. Address-book changes send no email and no transaction. A payout copies the recipient's address and email when it is created, so editing or deleting the recipient later cannot redirect it.

## Creating a payout

**Payouts** → **Request payout**: choose the **Payout chain** and **Payout currency**, then either **Find saved recipient** or **Enter destination** with a recipient email and address, and the **Payout amount (token units)**. Convert from USD yourself if needed; there is no price endpoint in this release. Owners, admins and project leads create requests; project managers read; project operators have no access.

At creation the server:

- Values the amount in USD with a fresh price (stablecoins at 1.00), rounded down to six places. Without a fresh price the request is refused.
- Checks the minimum: the project's **Minimum (USD)**, or `payout.minimumUsd` (default 1).
- Checks the **Hourly** and **Daily limit per recipient (USD)**: all unfinished requests for that recipient email in the project count against the limit, whatever their age, and processed payouts count within the rolling window.
- Reserves the amount against the hot wallet's live balance minus every unfinished payout on that wallet, chain and currency, across projects, so two requests cannot promise the same funds.
- Rejects a payout to the hot wallet itself.
- Refuses a duplicate: the same project, chain, currency, destination and amount within `payout.duplicateWindowSeconds` (default 300) returns a conflict, unless the request carries an `Idempotency-Key`. With a key, a repeat returns the original payout and a changed payload returns a conflict.

Amounts are exact decimal strings and cannot exceed the token's decimals.

## Approval

Every dashboard request needs an administrator's one-time code. A request made by an owner or admin starts as `pending-otp-verification`; one made by a project lead starts as `pending-approval`. In **Payout details** the administrator requests a code. The email states the amount, currency, chain and destination it approves. The administrator enters the **Approval code** and clicks **Approve payout**.

- Codes have `auth.otp.codeLength` digits (default 6), last `auth.otp.ttlSeconds` (default 600) and allow `auth.otp.maxVerifyAttempts` wrong entries (default 5). An administrator can request one code per minute and ten per hour. A new code for the same payout replaces the previous one.
- The code is bound to the administrator, the payout and its asset terms. Approval fetches a fresh price and rechecks the minimum, limits, wallet assignment and balance before consuming the code. A wrong code counts as an attempt; a consumed code cannot be reused.
- Owners and admins can **Reject payout** with an optional reason. The creator or an administrator can **Cancel payout** until the transaction is signed. Rejected and cancelled payouts release their reservations.

API payouts follow the project's automatic approval policy: when it is enabled and the fresh USD value is at or below the maximum, the payout is approved without a code and enters the queue. Otherwise it waits as `pending-approval` for a dashboard administrator. Automatic approval never overrides the minimum, limits or balance checks.

## Execution

A worker runs every `watcher.confirmationsIntervalSeconds` (default 15 seconds) while `watcher.enabled` is true and handles up to 20 payouts per pass. For each approved payout it locks the wallet, rechecks the approved terms and assignment, builds the transfer (native value or ERC-20 `transfer` on Robinhood Chain; a System Program transfer or an SPL `transferChecked` with recipient token account creation on Solana), signs it with the decrypted hot wallet key and stores the signed transaction encrypted, with its hash, before any broadcast. Signing is serialised with [sweeps](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md) on the same wallet. On Solana every payout carries a unique memo, so two identical payouts never share a signature.

The payout is marked `initiated` before the send. Broadcast goes to one RPC node with one attempt; an uncertain response is retried only by resending the identical bytes. Once the transaction is included and confirmed, the worker verifies the exact sender, recipient, asset and amount from the receipt and records the actual network fee. The approved amount and destination are never changed by the worker. If the signed transaction cannot be found or proved, the payout keeps its hash and reservation for manual review; it is not rebuilt with a new nonce or blockhash.

An inactive project, chain or wallet pauses new sends; confirmation of an already sent transaction continues. A pre-signing failure such as insufficient funds marks the payout `failed`; an RPC failure leaves it to retry.

## States

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending-otp-verification` | Created by an owner or admin; waiting for their code. |
| `pending-approval` | Created by a project lead or by the API above the automatic limit; waiting for an administrator. |
| `pending` | Approved; waiting for the worker. |
| `initiated` | Signed and a broadcast attempted. The hash is set; the outcome may still be uncertain. Cannot be cancelled. |
| `sent` | Included and confirmed on chain with matching proof. The network fee is recorded. |
| `processed` | Final pass after confirmation. Reservations are released. |
| `failed` | Pre-signing validation failed, or the transaction failed on chain. `failureReason` says why. |
| `rejected` | Refused by an administrator. |
| `cancelled` | Withdrawn by the creator or an administrator before signing. |

`processed`, `failed`, `rejected` and `cancelled` are terminal.

## Payout history

**Payout history** has two tabs, **Requests** and **Processed and closed**, with search over email, destination and transaction hash, status and date filters, and metrics for in-process, completed and total USD. **Payout details** shows the transaction hash, native network fee, confirmation and processing times and the webhook delivery summary, and polls every ten seconds while work is pending. API payouts appear here as well.

## Payout webhooks

Each transition writes one delivery per active endpoint in the same transaction as the state change. Events: `payout.pending-approval`, `payout.approved`, `payout.initiated`, `payout.sent`, `payout.processed`, `payout.failed`, `payout.rejected`, `payout.cancelled`. The payload carries the payout ID, network, token, amount, USD value, email, address, sender, transaction hash, status in upper case, timestamps and failure reason, plus the native fee once known. Deliveries can arrive more than once or out of order; deduplicate by payout ID, state and delivery ID. Headers, signing and retries are the same as for payments; see [Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md).

## Not in this release

Operator resolution of a signed transaction whose outcome stays unknown, and reconciliation after a deep chain reorganisation, are not implemented. Such payouts stay visible with their hash for manual review.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md

# Sweeps

Every customer payment, from a connected wallet or from any other wallet or exchange, arrives at the customer's deposit address and stays there until a sweep. A sweep is a transaction, signed by the project's hot wallet, for one deposit address and one currency: on Solana a call to the recv.fund program, on Robinhood Chain a call to your own merchant contract. It sends the balance to your registered settlement wallet minus the fee, which goes to the fee collector recorded in your registration in the same transaction. A sweep is the only way funds leave a deposit address. On Solana a token sweep also closes the deposit token account. On Robinhood Chain the first sweep of an address deploys its forwarder contract, which stays deployed for later sweeps.

The hot wallet pays the network fee, so it needs SOL or ETH. Deactivating your registration does not block sweeps. See [Funds sweeping](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/funds-sweeping.md) for the first run.

## The fee

The recv.fund fee is taken only here, at sweep, and never when a customer pays. It is `amount * feeBps / 10000`, rounded down, where `feeBps` is the rate copied into your registration when it was confirmed. The settlement wallet receives `amount - fee`. The rate cannot exceed 200 basis points (2%), and no function exists that changes it, or the fee collector, for an existing registration. recv.fund can change the terms only for registrations made afterwards.

If the fee collector cannot receive the fee, the fee goes to the settlement wallet, the chain emits `FeeRedirected`, and the sweep's `DepositSwept` event reports a fee of 0. On Robinhood Chain this covers a collector that rejects ETH, uses up the 200,000 gas allowance of the fee transfer, or is blocked by the token; on Solana a SOL fee that would leave the collector below rent exemption, or a frozen collector token account. A sweep that owes a fee on Robinhood Chain reverts with `InsufficientGas()` when too little gas is supplied.

## Settings

**Sweeps** → **Automatic sweep settings** shows the project's values, or the install defaults when nothing is overridden. **Use installation defaults** clears the overrides. Owners, admins and project leads change settings; other roles read.

| Field | Config key | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Minimum eligible balance (USD) | `sweep.activationUsd` | 5 | Non-negative, at most six decimals |
| Amount trigger (USD) | `sweep.amountUsd` | 50 | Positive |
| Address count trigger | `sweep.addressCount` | 25 | 1 to 10000 |
| Interval trigger (minutes) | `sweep.intervalMinutes` | 1440 | 1 to 525600 |
| Enable automatic sweeps when the scheduler is available | `sweep.enabled` | on | |
