The wallet signs one plain transfer of the quoted amount to the customer's deposit address; no recv.fund contract or program instruction runs and no fee is taken. It is recorded as a deposit and credited to the payment that was being paid. |
| Deposit | A transfer into a customer's deposit address, from a connected wallet at checkout or from any wallet or exchange. A transfer confirmed through the checkout page is credited to the payment that was paid; any other is matched to the open or partially filled payment whose current quote has the same currency and exact amount, otherwise to the customer's newest open or partially filled payment, and with none eligible it is recorded as an unmatched deposit under the customer. The fee is deducted later, at sweep. |
| Unmatched deposit | A confirmed deposit with no eligible payment to credit. It stays in the customer's history and in the ledger and is swept like any other balance. |
| Transaction (ledger) | Every on-chain transfer the install has verified, with hash, amounts, USD value at detection time and status `detected`, `confirmed` or `orphaned`. This release records every transfer with kind `deposit`; the kind `checkout-pay` belonged to the superseded program payment path and is not written any more. |
| Watcher | The set of schedulers in the API that discover deposits and recheck confirmations. They store their progress in the database so they resume where they stopped. |
| Missed payment report | A transaction hash you submit under Payments, Missed payments when a payment was not credited. The worker verifies the transaction on-chain and credits it through the normal path, or rejects it with a reason. |
| Test payment | A payment on a testnet install. The checkout page labels it and the checkout URL carries `test=true`. |

## Sweeps

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Sweep | Moving the whole balance of one currency at one deposit address to the settlement wallet, through the program on Solana or the merchant contract on Robinhood Chain. The fee is deducted at the registration's fixed rate and sent to the registration's fee collector in the same transaction. The transaction is signed by the project's hot wallet. See [Sweeps](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md) and [Funds sweeping](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/funds-sweeping.md). |
| Activation threshold | `sweep.activationUsd`, default 5 USD. A deposit balance below it is not eligible for an automatic sweep. Manual sweeps ignore it. |
| Sweep triggers | The conditions that start an automatic sweep for a project and chain: amount (`sweep.amountUsd`, default 50 USD across eligible balances), count (`sweep.addressCount`, default 25 eligible addresses) or time (`sweep.intervalMinutes`, default 1440). Precedence is amount, count, then time. |
| Manual sweep | A sweep queued from the dashboard for selected addresses and currencies. It bypasses the activation threshold, the triggers and the automatic-sweep switch. |
| Sweep status | `pending`, `sent`, `confirmed` or `failed`. `sent` means a broadcast was attempted; `confirmed` means the sweep's `DepositSwept` event was verified. |

## Payouts

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Payout | A transfer from the project's hot wallet to an address, in token units. It is a direct transfer and does not go through the program or any recv.fund contract. Created in the dashboard or by `POST /api/v1/withdrawal/merchant`. See [Payouts](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md). |
| Address book | Saved payout recipients per project: name, email, chain and address. A payout snapshots the recipient at creation, so later edits cannot redirect it. |
| Payout limits | USD limits per project, evaluated per recipient email: minimum, hourly, daily and auto-approve maximum. |
| Approval | Dashboard payouts always require an installation administrator to enter a one-time code sent by email. API payouts within the project's auto-approve limit are approved automatically; above it they wait for the same approval. SMTP must be configured. |
| Payout status | `pending-otp-verification`, `pending-approval`, `pending`, `initiated`, `sent`, `processed`, `failed`, `rejected` or `cancelled`. |
| Idempotency key | An optional value (`Idempotency-Key` header) on payout creation. Repeating the same request with the same key returns the original payout; the same key with changed fields is rejected. |

## Integration

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| API key | A 32-character hexadecimal key that authenticates a project's requests to the merchant API in the `API-Key` header. Created under Developers and shown once; only a hash is stored. Keys are rate limited per key. See [API keys](https://docs.recv.fund/features/api-keys.md) and [API integration](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/introduction.md). |
| Webhook endpoint | A URL in a project that receives a signed JSON POST on payment creation, payment state changes, confirmation progress and payout state changes. Each endpoint has a secret, shown once at creation or rotation. See [Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md). |
| Webhook signature | The `X-Recv-Signature` header: `sha256=` followed by the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the endpoint secret. `X-Payram-Signature` carries the same value. |
| Delivery | One attempt series for one event to one endpoint, identified by `X-Recv-Delivery`. Failed deliveries are retried on a fixed schedule; the last attempt and next attempt time are shown under Developers. |
| Event type | The `X-Recv-Event` header value: `payment.confirming`, `payment.filled`, `payment.partially-filled`, `payment.over-filled`, `payment.cancelled`, and `payout.<status>` for payouts. |


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks.md

# Networks and tokens

recv.fund supports two chains. Each exists as a mainnet and a testnet row in the install's chain catalog. `NETWORK_TYPE`, chosen at install time, selects which rows the install uses; the other rows are present but unused.

## Networks

| Chain | Code | Network type | Network | RPC endpoint seeded | Explorer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Solana | `SOLANA` | `mainnet` | mainnet-beta | `https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com` | `https://solscan.io` |
| Solana | `SOLANA` | `testnet` | devnet | `https://api.devnet.solana.com` | `https://solscan.io` with `cluster=devnet` |
| Robinhood Chain | `ROBINHOOD` | `mainnet` | chain id 4663 | `https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com` | `https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com` |
| Robinhood Chain | `ROBINHOOD` | `testnet` | chain id 46630 | `https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com` | `https://explorer.testnet.chain.robinhood.com` |

The chain code is what the API uses in `network` and `blockchainCode` fields. Robinhood Chain is an Arbitrum Orbit L2 (EVM-equivalent); Solana is its own family. The Robinhood Chain URLs and chain ids were checked against Robinhood's wallet network configuration page on 2026-09-26.

## RPC nodes

The seeded endpoints are public and free. They are active and not marked preferred. You can add up to ten nodes per chain under Settings, Nodes, mark one as preferred, and remove or disable the seeded ones. Every read validates the node's chain id (EVM) or genesis hash (Solana) before use, so a node on the wrong network cannot supply balances. Reads fall back to the next node on failure; signing and broadcasting use one node and never fall back. See [Node configuration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/node-configuration.md).

Nodes must retain the history the watchers need to catch up after downtime. On Robinhood Chain, ETH sent directly to a deposit address, by hand or from a connected wallet at checkout, is credited through any node. ETH that a smart contract (for example some exchange wallets) forwards to a deposit address inside another transaction is credited only through a node that supports `debug_traceTransaction` and `debug_traceBlockByHash` with the call tracer; the public Robinhood Chain endpoint and some providers' free plans do not. ERC-20 payments need neither.

## Tokens

| Currency | Chain | Network type | Standard | Token address | Decimals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| USDC | Solana | `mainnet` | SPL | `EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v` | 6 |
| USDT | Solana | `mainnet` | SPL | `Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB` | 6 |
| SOL | Solana | `mainnet` and `testnet` | native | none | 9 |
| USDC | Solana | `testnet` (devnet) | SPL | `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU` | 6 |
| USDG | Robinhood Chain | `mainnet` | ERC-20 | `0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168` | 6 |
| USDG | Robinhood Chain | `testnet` | ERC-20 | `0x7E955252E15c84f5768B83c41a71F9eba181802F` | 6 |
| ETH | Robinhood Chain | `mainnet` and `testnet` | native | none | 18 |

USDT is not seeded on Solana devnet, so a testnet install offers USDC and SOL on Solana and USDG and ETH on Robinhood Chain.

The USDC addresses match Circle's published list and the USDG addresses match Paxos's documentation; see [Links](https://docs.recv.fund/support/links.md). Token-2022 mints and extension mints are not supported on Solana. Once a merchant registration has started, a currency's token address and decimals cannot be edited; the currency can still be enabled or disabled.

Each project chooses which of these currencies to offer at checkout. A currency appears on the checkout page only if it is enabled for the project and the project has an active merchant registration on its chain.

## Native coins

SOL and ETH have two roles.

- Transaction fees. Every sweep and payout is signed by the project's hot wallet, which pays the network fee in the native coin. Keep the hot wallet funded. On Robinhood Chain the first sweep of a deposit address also deploys its forwarder contract, which costs more gas than later sweeps. On Solana, the first token deposit for a customer also needs rent for the deposit token account, which the sender's wallet normally pays (a wallet payment from the checkout page creates the account itself); the sweep closes that account and returns the rent to the hot wallet.
- Payment currencies. Both can be enabled for a project. Both can be paid from a connected wallet on the checkout page, as a plain transfer to the customer's deposit address, or sent to that address from any wallet or exchange.

Prices for SOL and ETH come from CoinGecko, cached for 60 seconds by default. The stablecoins are priced at exactly 1.00 USD.

## Confirmations

| Chain | Default confirmations | How it is counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solana | 1 | A transaction at `confirmed` commitment counts as 1; `finalized` counts as the configured threshold. |
| Robinhood Chain | 12 | Latest block minus the transaction's block, plus one. |

These are application defaults, not statements about chain finality. A project can override them per chain. A transfer below the threshold is recorded as detected, sends `payment.confirming` webhooks as its count rises, and adds no value to the payment until it reaches the threshold. Sweeps and payouts wait for the same threshold before they are marked confirmed.

## Program addresses

Each release ships these addresses, and the installation connects to the one for its network by itself after checking that the code matches the release (see [Node configuration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/node-configuration.md#recvfund-deployment)). You don't need to enter them. They are the program ID on Solana and the `RecvFundFactory` contract address on Robinhood Chain; each merchant creates its own merchant contract through that factory when it registers.

| Chain | Network | What | Address | Fee for new registrations | Fee collector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Solana | devnet | `recvfund` program | `FAZUvvc2anrhgkP6sVczAHp2wkFCfhzpFcbiBt1mVM8J` | 100 bps, taken at sweep | `GStZmhS72eX1euYiwQY9MaxahBopDBLGwfTtXPge3DK` |
| Robinhood Chain | testnet (46630) | `RecvFundFactory` contract | `0xDc055613c64a39ea6a9a2ad8c15D587381A12f8c` | 100 bps, taken at sweep | `0x74520411b6349b1A79f504D9b4717238Dbade236` |

Both were deployed on 2026-10-03. The fee rate and fee collector shown are the terms a registration made now receives; a registration keeps the terms it was created with. The Solana devnet program's config account is `5uLBoziU1on7DmPDyYPobgZhkFeWtjy91GW3HGWxFLcT`. The devnet program still has an upgrade authority, so treat it as provisional; the server refuses a mainnet program that has one. The Robinhood Chain contracts have no proxy and cannot be upgraded, and the factory source is verified on the Robinhood Chain testnet explorer.

The mainnet program and factory are not deployed yet.

Superseded, do not use: the Robinhood Chain testnet registry `0xBe4E003224977110100463EcC70D399bA0f1c9F8` and the Solana devnet program `G9u3a8P6T5RFsgQhjVC5Yw7oAUqURst5MQJi1rFVkzAt`, both deployed on 2026-09-30. They took a fee on checkout payments as well as on sweeps and are not accepted by the current server build.

The server checks the code at the address against the build it supports and reads the fee terms for new registrations and the fee cap before accepting it. After any merchant registration has started, the address cannot be replaced, because existing deposit addresses depend on it.

## Test funds

On a testnet install you need devnet SOL and Robinhood Chain testnet ETH in the hot wallet and in the wallet you test payments from.

- Devnet SOL can be requested with the Solana CLI (`solana airdrop`, with the CLI pointed at devnet) or from Solana's official devnet faucet.
- Robinhood Chain testnet ETH comes from Robinhood's official testnet faucet.
- Test USDC on devnet and test USDG on Robinhood Chain testnet are the mints and contracts listed above. How to obtain them is not covered here; check the issuer's documentation.

This documentation does not list faucet URLs. Use the faucet linked from each chain's official documentation.

# Change log

Short release notes are on the [What's new](https://docs.recv.fund/whats-new.md) page. This page is the full record.

Since 0.1.2, every change to recv.fund is published as a new version number, and a published version never changes. `--update` installs the newest version.

## 0.1.7 (2026-10-05)

- Setup is its own page (sidebar: **Setup**). It shows **Integration status**: live checks of the server, RPC nodes, the recv.fund contract, hot wallet fee balances, registrations, and sweeps, payouts and webhook deliveries that failed in the last seven days, each linked to the page that fixes it. The step-by-step guide follows on the same page.
- Every other page shows a reminder banner to owners and admins until setup is complete. The Overview page shows reporting only.

## 0.1.6 (2026-10-05)

- Hot wallet import accepts keys as wallets export them: the base58 private key from Phantom or Solflare, a Solana CLI keypair array, and an EVM key from MetaMask with or without `0x`.
- The setup guide always works on one project, and it no longer offers an installation-only view.

## 0.1.5 (2026-10-05)

- The installation connects to the recv.fund program (Solana) and factory contract (Robinhood Chain) by itself. Each release ships the addresses of its deployments; at startup and every five minutes, the server sets the one for each network that has none yet, after checking its code. An address that is already set is never changed.
- Nodes shows the recv.fund deployment as verified, or as connecting with the last error and a **Connect now** button. Another address can still be entered under **Use a different deployment (advanced)**.
- The **recv.fund contract** step of the setup guide is a check, not a task.

## 0.1.4 (2026-10-05)

- Dashboard typography and contrast: system fonts, clearer text colors, and the registration step summarized as three short facts.

## 0.1.3 (2026-10-05)

- The setup guide on the Overview page shows one step at a time for the selected project and network, with links to the right section of each page and back, **Check again**, and an explorable "How money moves" panel.
- Installer 0.1.3: `--http-bind` publishes the HTTP port on one address only, and `--site-url` sets the site URL without the prompt. See [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md).

## 0.1.2 (2026-10-05)

- The Overview page starts with a **Set up payments** guide covering the site URL, RPC nodes, contract, hot wallet, registration, currencies, a test payment and email.
- Every change is released as a new version. The installer looks up the newest version when it runs, instead of a version fixed in the installer.

## 2026-09: Initial release

The first public release of recv.fund. The mainnet factory and program are not deployed yet, so payments can be taken only on the test networks.

On 2026-10-03 the test network deployments were replaced by the payment model described below: customers pay their deposit address directly, the fee is taken only at sweep and is fixed per registration, and registration is one transaction. The Robinhood Chain testnet registry `0xBe4E003224977110100463EcC70D399bA0f1c9F8` and the Solana devnet program `G9u3a8P6T5RFsgQhjVC5Yw7oAUqURst5MQJi1rFVkzAt`, both deployed on 2026-09-30, are superseded. The current addresses are listed under [Networks and tokens](https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks.md#program-addresses).

### Chains and tokens

- Solana (`SOLANA`): USDC, USDT and SOL on mainnet; USDC and SOL on devnet.
- Robinhood Chain (`ROBINHOOD`): USDG and ETH on mainnet and testnet.
- Seeded public RPC endpoints and explorers per network. Up to ten RPC nodes per chain, with a preferred node and automatic failover for reads.
- Default confirmations of 1 on Solana and 12 on Robinhood Chain, with a per-project override.

### Installation

- One-line installer for mainnet or testnet: installs Docker if missing, asks for network type, Postgres (bundled or external) and HTTPS (Let's Encrypt or plain HTTP), generates secrets, runs migrations and starts the stack.
- Update, restart, status and reset operations from the same script.
- Compose stack of Caddy, API, web app, Redis and optional bundled Postgres, with dashboard, checkout and API on one origin.

### Accounts and projects

- Root account wizard at `/signup`; email and password login with session refresh.
- Team roles: owner, admin, project lead, project manager and project ops. Invitations with a temporary password.
- Projects with branding (logo, color, redirect URLs), enabled currencies, API keys, webhook endpoints and payout limits.
- Activity log of write and denied requests.
- Settings for site URL, SMTP, native coin pricing and WalletConnect project id.

### On-chain registration and wallets

- Merchant registration per project per chain in one transaction, signed in the browser with an injected wallet. The signing wallet becomes the admin; the cold wallet (settlement address), the sweeper, the fee rate and the fee collector are recorded on-chain. On Robinhood Chain the transaction creates the merchant's own contract (`MerchantVault`) through the recv.fund factory; on Solana it creates the merchant account of the recv.fund program.
- Settlement wallet, sweeper and active-flag updates, prepared by the server and signed by the admin wallet. The fee rate and fee collector of a registration cannot be changed.
- Hot wallets per chain family, generated or imported in the dashboard and stored encrypted. Balance reads on request.
- Deposit addresses derived from the merchant registration (Solana PDA, Robinhood Chain CREATE2 address of the merchant contract). No deposit keys on the server.

### Payments

- Payment links from the dashboard and `POST /api/v1/payment` from the API, with USD amounts, optional currency and network restriction, and expiry.
- Hosted checkout page with currency selection, exact quotes, deposit address and QR code, and wallet payment for every currency, SOL included. A wallet payment is one plain transfer from the customer's wallet to the customer's deposit address; no recv.fund contract or program instruction runs and no fee is taken.
- Deposit discovery per address and currency with resumable progress, matching to the eligible payment whose quote has the same currency and exact amount, otherwise the customer's newest eligible payment, and unmatched deposits kept under the customer. A wallet payment whose hash the checkout page submits is credited to the payment that was paid; one the page never reports is found by deposit discovery.
- Confirmation tracking with `payment.confirming` progress events, fill tolerance, and the states `OPEN`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED`, `FILLED`, `OVER_FILLED` and `CANCELLED`.
- Missed payment reports: submit a transaction hash for verification and credit.
- Payment history with search, filters, detail and CSV export.

### Sweeps

- Automatic sweeps per project and chain with an activation threshold and amount, count and time triggers.
- Manual sweeps of selected addresses and currencies.
- One fee, at most 2%, taken only at sweep at the rate fixed in the registration. If the fee collector cannot receive the fee, it goes to the settlement wallet and the sweep completes.
- Signed transactions are stored before broadcast and confirmed from the `DepositSwept` event.

### Payouts

- Payout requests from the dashboard and from `POST /api/v1/withdrawal/merchant`, in token units, from the project's hot wallet.
- Address book per project.
- USD limits per recipient email: minimum, hourly, daily and auto-approve maximum.
- Approval by a one-time code emailed to an administrator. Idempotency keys and duplicate detection.
- Payout lifecycle webhooks.

### API and webhooks

- Payments and payouts API with PayRam-compatible paths, field names and states, authenticated with the `API-Key` header.
- Public ticker (`GET /api/v1/ticker`) with the current USD price of every active currency.
- Signed webhooks (`X-Recv-Signature`, HMAC-SHA256) with a ten-attempt retry schedule, delivery history and manual redelivery.

### Analytics

- Dashboard with confirmed receipts, volume and payer activity per project and period.

### Not in this release

- WalletConnect on the checkout page and in registration. Only injected browser wallets are supported.
- Mainnet deployments of the Robinhood Chain factory and the Solana program.
- Low-balance email alerts for hot wallets.
- Operator mode (one install serving several merchants with a markup).
- Automatic reconciliation after a deep chain reorganisation.
- Token-2022 mints on Solana.

Source: https://docs.recv.fund/support/faq/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/support/faq.md

# FAQ

## Is recv.fund custodial?

No. recv.fund is software you run on your own server. Nothing we run is in the path of a payment. Every customer payment is a plain transfer from the customer's wallet to that customer's deposit address; no recv.fund contract or program instruction runs when a customer pays. The funds stay at the deposit address until your install sweeps them to the settlement wallet you registered.

A sweep can move funds from a deposit address only to your registered settlement wallet and to the fee collector recorded in your registration. No instruction or function takes a caller-supplied destination. Only a transaction signed by your admin wallet can change your settlement wallet. There is no pause or freeze function. On Solana the vendor authority cannot sign a sweep; on Robinhood Chain your merchant contract has no owner and recv.fund has no role in it. If the fee collector cannot receive a fee, the fee goes to your settlement wallet, so no account recv.fund controls can block a sweep.

recv.fund is non-custodial software; you remain responsible for your own legal obligations in your jurisdiction.

## What fee is charged, and where is it enforced?

One fee, a percentage of each sweep. Nothing is taken when a customer pays; the full amount arrives at the customer's deposit address. When your install sweeps a deposit address, the sweep sends the fee to the fee collector and the rest to your settlement wallet in the same transaction. The fee is `amount * rate / 10000`, rounded down, and the rate is at most 200 basis points (2%).

The rate and the fee collector are recorded in your registration on chain when the registration transaction is confirmed: in the `Merchant` account on Solana, in your own merchant contract on Robinhood Chain. Sweeps read them from there. Before you sign, the dashboard shows the rate under Nodes ("Fee for new registrations (basis points, taken at sweep)") and in the registration panel ("Fee: N bps of each sweep").

There is no subscription and no setup fee. You pay for your own server and the network fees of sweeps and payouts.

## Can the fee change?

Not for a registered merchant. Your rate and fee collector are copied into your registration when it is created, and no instruction or function exists that changes them afterwards, for you or for recv.fund. recv.fund can change the terms only for registrations made after the change (`set_fee_terms` on the Solana program, `setFeeTerms` on the Robinhood Chain factory), and only up to the 200 basis points (2%) maximum compiled into the code.

These guarantees hold as long as the code itself cannot be replaced. The Robinhood Chain contracts have no proxy and cannot be upgraded; a change ships as a new factory, and merchant contracts created by the old one keep working unchanged. The Solana devnet program still has an upgrade authority and is provisional. The server refuses a Solana mainnet program that still has an upgrade authority, and the mainnet program is not deployed yet.

## What happens if my server is offline?

Payments still arrive. A customer who already has a deposit address can send to it whether or not your server is running, and the funds stay at that address. The checkout page itself is served by your server, so it is not available while the server is down.

What stops is bookkeeping and sweeping. When the server is back:

- The deposit watcher resumes from its per-address progress and credits every deposit it missed, including wallet payments whose hash the checkout page could not submit.
- Detected transfers continue counting confirmations.
- Queued webhooks and queued sweeps and payouts resume; a webhook whose delivery lease expired is retried.

The deposit watcher keeps its position in the database and advances it only after a page has been fully processed, so a crash mid-page replays that page safely. The RPC nodes you use must retain enough history for the catch-up. Payments whose expiry passed while the server was down are cancelled by the expiry scheduler; see the expiry question below for how later transfers are matched.

If a payment is still missing afterwards, report its transaction hash under Payments, Missed payments.

## What if I lose the AES key?

`AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `/opt/recvfund/.env` encrypts every secret in the database: hot wallet private keys, webhook secrets, the SMTP password and the session signing secrets. Without it those secrets cannot be recovered and there is no key export.

Deposit addresses and settlement are not affected, because no deposit key exists and the settlement wallet is yours. Funds at deposit addresses can still be swept: create a new hot wallet, assign it to the project, and update the sweeper on-chain with your admin wallet. Back up `.env` together with the database; see [What to back up](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction.md).

## Can I change the settlement wallet?

Yes. Under Wallets, Deposit wallets, prepare a settlement update for the registration. The server returns an unsigned transaction; you sign it with the admin wallet that registered, and the server confirms it on-chain. Only the admin wallet can do this. Deposit addresses do not change, because they are derived from the merchant id and the customer reference, not from the settlement wallet.

## What if a customer underpays or overpays?

The payment is valued at the confirmed amount received.

- Below the requested amount by more than the fill tolerance (0.01 USD by default): `PARTIALLY_FILLED`. A later deposit from the same customer is matched to it and can bring it to `FILLED`. Partially filled payments do not expire automatically.
- Within the tolerance: `FILLED`.
- Above the tolerance: `OVER_FILLED`. The whole amount is credited and is swept to your settlement wallet like any other deposit; nothing is returned automatically.

Each state is sent once as a webhook. The checkout page asks for an exact token amount from a quote and states the currency and network; funds sent in another currency or on another network are not credited to that payment.

## What happens when a payment expires?

An `OPEN` payment past its expiry (24 hours by default) becomes `CANCELLED` and a `payment.cancelled` webhook is sent. The checkout page no longer offers a quote or a wallet payment for it.

Funds can still arrive afterwards. A wallet payment whose hash the checkout page submits for that payment, or a transfer that was already detected before cancellation, is credited to the cancelled payment and can move it to a filled state. Any other new deposit to the customer's address after cancellation is not matched to a cancelled payment; it is credited to an open payment of the customer if there is one (preferring one whose current quote has the same currency and exact amount, otherwise the newest), or recorded as an unmatched deposit under the customer. Unmatched deposits are swept like any other balance.

## How do refunds work?

There is no refund feature. Payments arrive at deposit addresses, which have no key and can only be swept to your settlement wallet, and your settlement wallet is not controlled by the server.

If you decide to return funds, the mechanism the software provides is a payout: fund the project's hot wallet with the token, then create a payout to the customer's address from the dashboard or the API. Payouts are subject to the project's limits and approval. See [Payouts](https://docs.recv.fund/features/payouts.md).

## Is there KYC?

No identity verification is built in, and there is no account with recv.fund. Merchants remain responsible for their own legal obligations, including any customer verification their jurisdiction requires.

## Which wallets work on the checkout page?

Injected browser wallets: EVM wallets on Robinhood Chain and Phantom- or Solflare-compatible wallets on Solana. Every currency can be paid from a connected wallet, SOL included: the wallet signs one plain transfer of the quoted amount to the customer's deposit address, with no approval step. WalletConnect is not implemented yet.

Customers without a browser wallet, or paying from an exchange, send to the deposit address shown on the page or in its QR code. The QR code contains the address; the customer must use the currency and network stated on the page. Both ways the funds arrive at the same address.

## Is testnet supported?

Yes. Install with `--testnet` and the install runs against Solana devnet and Robinhood Chain testnet with the test tokens listed in [Networks and tokens](https://docs.recv.fund/support/networks.md). Every payment on such an install is a test payment: the checkout page labels it and the checkout URL carries `test=true`. Use a testnet install first.

## Can I switch between mainnet and testnet?

No. The network type is written to `.env` at install time and every chain, currency, registration and address belongs to it. Changing it requires a reset, which removes the containers, images and data. Run a second install on another server for the other network.

## How do I update?

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/recv-fund/recvfund-scripts/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --update
```

The script moves the installation to the newest released version, runs database migrations against the new image and then swaps the containers. Every change to recv.fund is published as a new version number, and a published version never changes, so the version in `IMAGE_TAG` in `/opt/recvfund/.env` tells you exactly what you run. The API refuses to start with unapplied migrations, which is why migrations run first. The same operation is option 2 in the script's menu. See [Script usage](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/script-usage.md).

## How do I stop the installation?

From `/opt/recvfund`, run `docker compose -p recvfund --profile db stop`. Start it again with `start`. Your data stays in place. Don't use `--reset` to stop: it deletes the containers, images and data. See [Stopping and starting](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/advanced-setup.md#stopping-and-starting).

## How do I back up?

Three things:

1. The database. With the bundled Postgres: `docker compose -p recvfund exec postgres pg_dump -U recv recv > backup.sql` from `/opt/recvfund`. With an external Postgres, use its own backup.
2. The `api-uploads` volume, which holds project logos.
3. `/opt/recvfund/.env`, in particular `AES_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

Restore is the reverse. See [What to back up](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction.md).

## What if the hot wallet runs out of native coin?

Sweeps and payouts need SOL or ETH for network fees. A sweep or payout that cannot be funded fails before it is signed and is shown as failed with the reason; nothing is broadcast. Top up the hot wallet and queue the sweep again or create the payout again. There is no low-balance alert in this release, so check the balance under Wallets, Hot wallets.

## Is a transfer straight to my settlement wallet credited?

No. The server credits only transfers into deposit addresses. A wallet payment from the checkout page is such a transfer. A customer must pay through the checkout page or send to their deposit address.

## Where do I get help?

Email `hello@recv.fund`. Read the [Deployment guide](https://docs.recv.fund/deployment-guide/introduction.md) and the [Onboarding guide](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/introduction.md) first, and include your server's OS version, the installer flags and the installer output. Report security issues to the same address with "Security" in the subject line. More links are on the [Links](https://docs.recv.fund/support/links.md) page.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/create-payment/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/create-payment.md

# Create payment

```
POST /api/v1/payment
```

Creates one payment for a USD amount and returns the checkout URL to send the customer to. The customer record is created or reused by `customerID`; the payment gets a new `reference_id` every time. No price lookup, address derivation or chain transaction happens at creation, so the call is fast and does not depend on an RPC node.

Headers: `API-Key`, `Content-Type: application/json`.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST https://<your-site>/api/v1/payment \
  -H "API-Key: 811b12035f0dfa8ffd62296df3c98b27" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "customerEmail": "a@example.com",
    "customerID": "1234",
    "amountInUSD": "50",
    "invoiceID": "INV-0090",
    "expire": "2026-09-30T12:00:00Z",
    "currency": "USDC",
    "network": "SOLANA"
  }'
```

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerEmail` | string | yes | A valid email address, at most 320 characters. Stored lowercased and trimmed; an existing customer's email is updated. |
| `customerID` | string | yes | Your identifier for the customer. Non-blank, at most 128 characters, trimmed. One customer per id per project. |
| `amountInUSD` | string or number | yes | Positive. At most 18 integer digits and 6 fractional digits, decimal notation only (`"12.5"`, `12.5`). A JSON number is parsed without precision loss; use a string when your serializer cannot preserve large values. Exponent notation in a string is rejected. |
| `invoiceID` | string | no | Your label for this payment. Non-blank, at most 128 characters. Echoed as `invoiceID` in status and `invoice_id` in webhooks. Not unique and not an idempotency key. |
| `expire` | string | no | ISO 8601 date-time with a time part and a timezone (`Z` or `+hh:mm`), in the future. Default: now plus `payment.expiryHours` (24 hours; 1 to 8760). An open payment that reaches this time becomes `CANCELLED`. |
| `currency` | string | no | Restrict the payment to one currency code (`^[A-Z0-9]{1,16}$`), for example `USDC`. Must be enabled for the project on an active chain of the install's network. If the code exists on more than one chain, `network` is required. |
| `network` | string | no | `SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`. Restricts the payment to one chain. Requires `currency`. |

A restriction fixes the currency and chain the customer can pay with; the checkout page and the deposit options endpoint show only that one. Without a restriction, the customer chooses among the project's enabled currencies whose chain has an active merchant registration.

## Response

`201 Created`

```json
{
  "host": "https://pay.example.com",
  "reference_id": "c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470",
  "url": "https://pay.example.com/payments?reference_id=c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470&host=https%3A%2F%2Fpay.example.com"
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | string | The site URL of this install, as configured under Settings. |
| `reference_id` | string | Version 4 UUID identifying the payment in every other call and webhook. |
| `url` | string | The hosted checkout page. `host` is URL-encoded in the query string. On a testnet install the URL ends with `&test=true`. |

Creation also queues a `payment.open` webhook for every active endpoint of the project.

## Errors

| Status | `code` | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | A field fails validation (see constraints above); the body is not JSON or `Content-Type` is not `application/json`; `network` given without `currency`; the requested currency is not enabled for this project and network; the currency code exists on more than one chain and `network` is missing; `expire` is not in the future. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Invalid API key. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | The customer with this `customerID` is inactive; or the install's site URL is not configured or invalid. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Per-key limit exhausted. |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | `payment.expiryHours` or the rate-limit setting is invalid, or Redis is unreachable. |

## Notes

- Merchant registration on chain is not required to create a payment, but a chain is offered at checkout only when the project has an active registration on it. See [Merchant registration](https://docs.recv.fund/onboarding-guide/merchant-registration.md).
- Concurrent requests for the same new `customerID` create one customer and one payment each.
- The request, customer change, payment and webhook row are one transaction. A failure leaves nothing behind.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md

# Deposit options

```
GET /api/v1/blockchain-currency/reference/{reference_id}
```

Returns the currencies available for this payment: the project's enabled currencies on active chains of the install's network that have an active merchant registration, narrowed by the `currency` and `network` restrictions given at creation. For each one, `customerAddress` is the receiving address if the customer already has an active deposit address on that chain, or empty.

Headers: `API-Key`.

## Request

```bash
curl https://<your-site>/api/v1/blockchain-currency/reference/c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470 \
  -H "API-Key: 811b12035f0dfa8ffd62296df3c98b27"
```

| Parameter | In | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference_id` | path | Version 4 UUID from create payment. |

## Response

`200 OK`, a JSON array. The array is empty when the payment is filled, over-filled, cancelled, expired, or its customer is inactive.

```json
[
  {
    "id": 3,
    "blockchainCode": "SOLANA",
    "network": "Solana",
    "currencyCode": "USDC",
    "currency": "USD Coin",
    "customerAddress": "",
    "tokenAddress": "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v",
    "standard": "spl",
    "walletPrecision": 6,
    "family": "solana",
    "recommended": true,
    "mostUsed": false,
    "blockchainID": 1,
    "currencyID": 3
  },
  {
    "id": 7,
    "blockchainCode": "ROBINHOOD",
    "network": "Robinhood Chain",
    "currencyCode": "USDG",
    "currency": "Global Dollar",
    "customerAddress": "0x2f1a4c8e9b7d6e5f4a3b2c1d0e9f8a7b6c5d4e3f",
    "tokenAddress": "0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168",
    "standard": "erc20",
    "walletPrecision": 6,
    "family": "evm",
    "recommended": true,
    "mostUsed": false,
    "blockchainID": 2,
    "currencyID": 7
  }
]
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | Currency id. Same value as `currencyID`. |
| `blockchainCode` | string | `SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`. The value to send to [Assign deposit address](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address.md). |
| `network` | string | Display name of the chain. |
| `currencyCode` | string | Currency code, for example `USDC`. |
| `currency` | string | Display name of the currency. |
| `customerAddress` | string | The address to send this currency to, or `""` if no active deposit address exists for the customer on this chain yet. For an SPL token this is the token account (the mint's associated token account owned by the customer's deposit account), not the deposit account itself. For native and ERC-20 currencies it is the deposit address. |
| `tokenAddress` | string | Mint or contract address. `native` for SOL; the zero address `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` for ETH. |
| `standard` | string | `native`, `spl` or `erc20`. |
| `walletPrecision` | integer | Decimal places of the currency. |
| `family` | string | `solana` or `evm`. |
| `recommended` | boolean | `true` for stablecoins. |
| `mostUsed` | boolean | Always `false`. Usage ranking is not implemented. |
| `blockchainID` | integer | Chain id in this install's catalog. Also the `chainID` value for the checkout `confirm` endpoint. |
| `currencyID` | integer | Currency id. Also the `currencyID` value for the checkout `select` endpoint. |

Order follows the catalog sort order, then currency id. Inactive deposit addresses are not reported.

## Errors

| Status | `code` | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | `reference_id` is not a version 4 UUID. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Invalid API key. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | No payment with this reference id in the key's project. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Per-key limit exhausted. |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | Rate-limit setting invalid or Redis unreachable. |

## Notes

- A deposit address is permanent per customer and chain. Once assigned, on this payment or an earlier one, every option on that chain reports it.
- Deposit addresses are derived from your on-chain merchant registration. No private key for them exists on any server. See [Customer deposit wallets](https://docs.recv.fund/features/customer-deposit-wallets.md).
- No RPC call is made by this endpoint.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/assign-deposit-address.md

# Assign deposit address

```
POST /api/v1/deposit-address/reference/{reference_id}
```

Derives the customer's permanent deposit address on the given chain, stores it, and selects that chain for this payment. Use it when you show a deposit address yourself instead of sending the customer to the checkout page. The address is the same for every future payment by this customer on this chain.

Headers: `API-Key`, `Content-Type: application/json`.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST https://<your-site>/api/v1/deposit-address/reference/c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470 \
  -H "API-Key: 811b12035f0dfa8ffd62296df3c98b27" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"blockchain_code": "SOLANA"}'
```

| Field | In | Type | Required | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference_id` | path | string | yes | Version 4 UUID from create payment. |
| `blockchain_code` | body | string | yes | `SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`. Must be a chain present in [Deposit options](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md) for this payment. |

## Response

`200 OK`

```json
{
  "id": 324,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-22T06:53:42.419Z",
  "Address": "9xQeWvG816bUx9EPjHmaT23yvVM2ZWbrrpZb9PusVFin",
  "Family": "solana",
  "Status": "active",
  "MemberID": 271,
  "BlockchainFamilyID": 1
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | Deposit address record id. |
| `createdAt` | string | ISO 8601 time the address was first assigned. Earlier than the request when the address already existed. |
| `Address` | string | The canonical deposit account: the program-derived address (PDA) on Solana, the CREATE2 address computed by your merchant contract on Robinhood Chain. For native SOL and ETH this is where the customer sends funds. |
| `Family` | string | `solana` or `evm`. |
| `Status` | string | `active` or `dormant`. |
| `MemberID` | integer | Internal customer id (not your `customerID`). |
| `BlockchainFamilyID` | integer | Chain id in this install's catalog. |

The PascalCase keys are PayRam's and are kept for compatibility.

## Which address to show the customer

`Address` is the deposit account. For an SPL token on Solana (USDC, USDT) the customer must send to the token account, which is a different address: read `customerAddress` for that currency from [Deposit options](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/deposit-options.md) after assignment. For USDG on Robinhood Chain and for native SOL and ETH, `customerAddress` equals `Address`.

Assignment selects only the chain. It does not select a currency and does not create a price quote. The first confirmed transfer sets the payment's currency. A quote (the exact token amount for the USD value) is only produced by the checkout `select` endpoint; for stablecoins the token amount equals the USD amount.

## Errors

| Status | `code` | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | `reference_id` is not a version 4 UUID; `blockchain_code` is missing or not `SOLANA`/`ROBINHOOD`; the chain is not available for this payment (not enabled, no active merchant registration, or excluded by the payment's restriction). |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Invalid API key. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | No payment with this reference id in the key's project. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | The payment is filled, over-filled, cancelled or expired, or its customer or project is inactive; the chain differs from the currently selected one and a transfer has already been detected; the payment or chain availability changed during the request (retry). |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Per-key limit exhausted. |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | Address derivation could not be completed, the rate-limit setting is invalid, or Redis is unreachable. Nothing is stored on failure. |

## Notes

- Repeating the call with the same chain is safe and returns the same address. Repeating it with a different chain clears any checkout quote and selected currency on the payment; after a transfer has been detected the chain can no longer change.
- The address is derived from your on-chain merchant registration and the customer's stored reference; the merchant registration on that chain must be active. No private key for the address exists anywhere.
- No transaction is sent, and no funds move, by this call. Funds arriving at the address are detected by the deposit watcher and credited when confirmed; they are moved to your settlement wallet by a [sweep](https://docs.recv.fund/features/sweeps.md).


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status.md

# Payment status

```
GET /api/v1/payment/reference/{reference_id}
```

Reads one payment. This is the call to make before fulfilling an order: a webhook tells you something changed, this endpoint tells you the current state from your own server. The read is served from the database; it makes no RPC call and never changes the payment.

Headers: `API-Key`.

## Request

```bash
curl https://<your-site>/api/v1/payment/reference/c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470 \
  -H "API-Key: 811b12035f0dfa8ffd62296df3c98b27"
```

| Parameter | In | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference_id` | path | Version 4 UUID from create payment. |

## Response

`200 OK`

```json
{
  "referenceID": "c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470",
  "invoiceID": "INV-0090",
  "customerID": "1234",
  "customerEmail": "a@example.com",
  "amountInUSD": "50.000000",
  "paymentState": "FILLED",
  "currency": "USDC",
  "network": "SOLANA",
  "filledAmount": "50",
  "filledAmountInUSD": "50.000000",
  "depositAddress": "4Nd1mYw9zqXxq2Vb7Lr8KfJ3sT6uHc1pQe9RaBwDgF2h",
  "confirmationCurrent": 1,
  "confirmationRequired": 1,
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-23T06:53:42.419Z",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-22T06:53:42.419Z",
  "merchantName": "Project One",
  "testMode": false
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `referenceID` | string | The payment's reference id. |
| `invoiceID` | string | Your `invoiceID` from creation, or `""`. |
| `customerID` | string | Your `customerID` from creation. |
| `customerEmail` | string | The customer's current email address. |
| `amountInUSD` | string | Requested amount, six decimals. |
| `paymentState` | string | `OPEN`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED`, `FILLED`, `OVER_FILLED` or `CANCELLED`. See [Payment states](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/index.md). |
| `currency` | string | The selected currency code, or the restricting currency from creation, or `""` when neither is set. |
| `network` | string | The selected chain code, or the restricting chain from creation, or `""`. |
| `filledAmount` | string | Confirmed amount in units of the selected currency (`"0"` until a currency is selected). Not padded to the currency's decimals. |
| `filledAmountInUSD` | string | Confirmed amount in USD, six decimals. Includes transfers in any currency credited to this payment. |
| `depositAddress` | string | The receiving address for the selected currency (the token account for SPL tokens), the deposit account when a chain is selected but no currency yet, or `""`. |
| `confirmationCurrent` | integer | The lowest confirmation count across the payment's non-orphaned transfers. `0` with no transfers. |
| `confirmationRequired` | integer | The selected or restricting chain's confirmation threshold. `0` when no chain is set. |
| `expiresAt` | string or null | ISO 8601 expiry. |
| `createdAt` | string | ISO 8601 creation time. |
| `merchantName` | string | The project name. |
| `testMode` | boolean | `true` on a testnet install. |

Amounts are strings. Do not parse `amountInUSD` or `filledAmountInUSD` into a binary floating-point number before comparing them.

## Errors

| Status | `code` | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | `reference_id` is not a version 4 UUID. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Invalid API key. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | No payment with this reference id in the key's project. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Per-key limit exhausted. |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | Rate-limit setting invalid or Redis unreachable. |

## Polling

Webhooks are the intended way to learn about changes; poll this endpoint as a fallback or to confirm a webhook. The per-key limit is 300 requests per minute by default across every keyed endpoint, so polling many open payments every few seconds will exhaust it. The hosted checkout page polls its own public endpoint, which is limited per IP address and does not count against your key.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/webhook/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/webhook.md

# Payment webhook

Your server registers one or more endpoint URLs per project in the dashboard under Developers, section Webhook endpoints ([Webhooks](https://docs.recv.fund/features/webhooks.md)). Each endpoint gets its own secret, shown once at creation and on rotation. Every active endpoint of a project receives every payment event and every [payout event](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payouts-api.md) of that project.

Delivery rows are written in the same database transaction as the payment change, so an event is never lost between the change and the queue. A worker sends them; `SEND_WEBHOOKS=false` in the install's `.env` stops all sending without discarding the queue.

## Delivery

```
POST <your endpoint URL>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Recv-Signature: sha256=<hex>
X-Payram-Signature: sha256=<hex>
X-Recv-Event: payment.filled
X-Recv-Delivery: 1042
```

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Recv-Signature` | `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the exact request body, keyed with the endpoint's secret string. |
| `X-Payram-Signature` | The same value, for handlers written against PayRam. Note that PayRam keys its HMAC with the project API key; recv.fund keys it with the endpoint secret. |
| `X-Recv-Event` | The event name (table below). |
| `X-Recv-Delivery` | The delivery id, a decimal integer as a string. Stable across every retry of the same delivery. |

Endpoint URLs must be `http:` or `https:` with no credentials or fragment. They may be on your internal network.

## Events

| `X-Recv-Event` | Payload `status` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payment.open` | `OPEN` | The payment was created. |
| `payment.confirming` | `OPEN` | A transfer's confirmation count changed. One delivery per newly observed count per transfer; `confirmation_current` and `confirmation_required` carry the progress. |
| `payment.filled` | `FILLED` | Confirmed funds are within the fill tolerance of the requested amount. |
| `payment.partially-filled` | `PARTIALLY_FILLED` | Confirmed funds are below the requested amount. |
| `payment.over-filled` | `OVER_FILLED` | Confirmed funds exceed the requested amount. |
| `payment.cancelled` | `CANCELLED` | The payment expired while open or was cancelled from the dashboard. |

Flow: `OPEN` → one `payment.confirming` per confirmation step → `FILLED`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED` or `OVER_FILLED`; or `OPEN` → `CANCELLED`. A transfer confirmed after cancellation still produces a filled-state event. A partially filled payment can later become filled or over-filled.

## Payload

```json
{
  "customer_id": "1234",
  "invoice_id": "INV-0090",
  "reference_id": "c80f5363-0397-4761-aa1a-3155c3a21470",
  "status": "FILLED",
  "amount": "50.000000",
  "currency": "USDC",
  "network": "SOLANA",
  "filled_amount": "50.000000",
  "filled_amount_in_usd": "50.000000",
  "sponsored_amount": "0",
  "sponsored_amount_in_usd": "0",
  "timestamp": 1758524022,
  "payment_info": [
    {
      "source_address": "7a2CkQ1v8mT5yRbGxWn3uHs9dLp4eJf6cVa2NzKq8YtB",
      "transaction_hash": "5KjP2n8vQ4wR7tY1uI3oA6sD9fG2hJ4kL7zX0cV5bN8mQ1wE3rT6yU9iO2pA5sD8f",
      "destination_address": "4Nd1mYw9zqXxq2Vb7Lr8KfJ3sT6uHc1pQe9RaBwDgF2h",
      "block_number": 301234567,
      "kind": "deposit",
      "currency_id": 3,
      "amount_raw": "50000000",
      "fee_raw": null,
      "status": "confirmed"
    }
  ],
  "confirmation_current": 1,
  "confirmation_required": 1
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `customer_id` | string | Your `customerID`. |
| `invoice_id` | string | Your `invoiceID`, or `""`. |
| `reference_id` | string | The payment's reference id. |
| `status` | string | `OPEN`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED`, `FILLED`, `OVER_FILLED` or `CANCELLED`. |
| `amount` | string | Requested USD amount. |
| `currency` | string | Selected currency code, or `""` before selection. |
| `network` | string | Chain code of the selected chain (or, for `payment.confirming`, of the transfer's chain), or `""`. |
| `filled_amount` | string | Confirmed amount in units of the selected currency, padded to its decimals. `"0"` before selection. |
| `filled_amount_in_usd` | string | Confirmed USD amount, six decimals. |
| `sponsored_amount` | string | Always `"0"`. Kept for PayRam field compatibility. |
| `sponsored_amount_in_usd` | string | Always `"0"`. |
| `timestamp` | integer | Unix time in seconds when the event was recorded. |
| `payment_info` | array | Up to 100 transfers recorded against this payment, oldest first, including transfers not yet confirmed. |
| `payment_info[].source_address` | string | Sending address. |
| `payment_info[].transaction_hash` | string | Transaction hash or Solana signature. |
| `payment_info[].destination_address` | string | Receiving address: the customer's deposit address, or for an SPL token its token account. A wallet checkout payment is a transfer to the same address. |
| `payment_info[].block_number` | integer | Block or slot. |
| `payment_info[].kind` | string | `deposit`. Every transfer, including a wallet checkout payment, is a transfer to a deposit address. The value `checkout-pay` belonged to the superseded program payment path and is not written by this release. |
| `payment_info[].currency_id` | integer | Catalog id of the transferred currency. |
| `payment_info[].amount_raw` | string | Transferred amount in base units of that currency. The full amount arrives at the deposit address. |
| `payment_info[].fee_raw` | string or null | `null`. No fee is taken when a customer pays; the fee is taken at sweep. |
| `payment_info[].status` | string | `detected`, `confirmed` or `orphaned`. |
| `confirmation_current` | integer | For `payment.confirming`, the transfer's new count. Otherwise the lowest count across transfers, `0` with none. |
| `confirmation_required` | integer | The chain's threshold, `0` when no chain is set. |

All amounts are strings. The payload is a snapshot taken when the event was recorded and does not change on retry.

## Verifying the signature

Compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request bytes with the endpoint secret, prefix `sha256=`, and compare with `X-Recv-Signature` in constant time. Read the raw body before any JSON parsing or re-serialization; a re-serialized body will not match.

```js
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
import express from 'express';

const secret = process.env.RECV_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
const app = express();

app.post('/webhooks/recv', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }), (req, res) => {
  const expected = Buffer.from(
    `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', secret).update(req.body).digest('hex')}`,
  );
  const given = Buffer.from(req.get('X-Recv-Signature') ?? '');
  if (given.length !== expected.length || !timingSafeEqual(given, expected)) {
    return res.status(401).end();
  }

  const deliveryId = req.get('X-Recv-Delivery');
  const event = JSON.parse(req.body.toString('utf8'));
  // 1. If deliveryId has been processed, return 200 without doing anything.
  // 2. Record deliveryId, then handle event.status for event.reference_id.
  res.status(200).end();
});
```

After a secret rotation the next attempt of every pending delivery is signed with the new secret. Keep the old secret accepted only for as long as you need to drain in-flight retries.

## Retries

Only an HTTP 2xx response counts as delivered. A 3xx is not followed and counts as a failure, as does any other status, a connection error, or no response within `webhook.timeoutMs` (default 60000 ms; 100 to 60000). The response body is discarded.

Failed attempts are retried on `webhook.retryScheduleSeconds`. The default gives ten attempts in total:

| Attempt | Delay after the previous failure |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | immediate |
| 2 | 2 s |
| 3 | 4 s |
| 4 | 30 min |
| 5 | 1 h |
| 6 | 2 h |
| 7 | 4 h |
| 8 | 8 h |
| 9 | 24 h |
| 10 | 48 h |

After the last attempt the delivery is marked `failed`. The dashboard shows each delivery's status, attempt count, last HTTP result and next attempt time, and lets an owner, admin or project lead retry a failed delivery by hand, which restarts the schedule. An endpoint that is disabled pauses its deliveries; enabling it makes overdue ones eligible again. An endpoint added later does not receive events recorded before it existed.

The payment's `webhookStatus` in the dashboard summarizes its deliveries: `pending` if any is pending, otherwise `failed` if any failed, otherwise `received`.

## Handling deliveries

- **Deduplicate on `X-Recv-Delivery`.** Delivery is at least once: your handler may run before a timeout or crash on the sending side makes the same delivery retry. Store the id before doing work, and answer 200 for an id you have already seen.
- **Tolerate out-of-order events.** Retries of an old event can arrive after a newer one. Make decisions from `status` and the state you already hold, or read [Payment status](https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/payment-status.md) after receiving an event.
- **Answer quickly.** Queue the work and return 200; the 60 second timeout is the maximum, not a target.
- **Do not trust the body alone for fulfillment.** The signature proves the body came from your install. Reading the status endpoint from your server proves the current state.
- **Use `reference_id`, not `invoice_id`, as the key.** `invoice_id` is your label and may repeat.


---
Source: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/ticker/
Markdown: https://docs.recv.fund/api-integration/payments-api/ticker.md

# Ticker

Lists every active currency on active chains for the installation's network type, with the current USD price of one unit. Use it to show the amount a customer will send, as the demo store does for deposit-address payments.

```bash
curl https://<your-site>/api/v1/ticker
```

No API key is needed. The endpoint is rate limited per IP address with the checkout limit (`rateLimit.checkout.perMinute`).

## Response

`200` with an array:

```json
[
  {
    "blockchainCode": "SOLANA",
    "currencyCode": "USDC",
    "tokenAddress": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
    "standard": "spl",
    "walletPrecision": 6,
    "family": "solana",
    "price": "1.0"
  },
  {
    "blockchainCode": "ROBINHOOD",
    "currencyCode": "ETH",
    "tokenAddress": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "standard": "native",
    "walletPrecision": 18,
    "family": "evm",
    "price": "3421.17"
  }
]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blockchainCode` | string | `SOLANA` or `ROBINHOOD`. |
| `currencyCode` | string | For example `USDC`, `USDG`, `SOL`, `ETH`. |
| `tokenAddress` | string | Mint or contract address; `native` for SOL and the zero address for ETH. |
| `standard` | string | `native`, `spl` or `erc20`. |
| `walletPrecision` | number | Decimal places of one unit. |
| `family` | string | `solana` or `evm`. |
| `price` | string | USD price of one unit. Stablecoins are `"1.0"`; they are catalog pegs, not live market prices. |

## Errors

| Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | A current price for any listed currency is unavailable. The whole request fails; prices are never omitted or replaced with stale values. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | The per-IP limit for the current minute is exhausted. |
